Title: GDB Holdings buys 51pct stakes in two firms for RM81.6mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: GDB Holdings Bhd is acquiring 51 per cent stakes in two construction companies for RM81.6 million.
In a bourse filing, GDB said it will acquire 51 per cent of Bina Tegas Sdn Bhd for RM66.51 million and 51 per cent of BT Borneo Engineering Sdn Bhd for RM15.09 million.
GDB will satisfy the RM81.6 million consideration through RM40.8 million cash and RM40.8 million of new GDB shares.
The cash portion will be funded through a proposed private placement, while the consideration shares will be issued at 42.1 sen each.
The placement involves up to 309.38 million new GDB shares, representing not more than 30 per cent of its issued share capital.
GDB is also proposing a renounceable rights issue of up to 205.36 million new shares, together with 205.36 million free warrants.
This is based on one rights share for every seven existing shares held.
It noted that the vendors, Bina Tegas Sdn Bhd and BT Borneo Engineering Sdn Bhd, guaranteed a combined net profit of at least RM45 million and an order book of RM400 million by end-2028.
It said the acquisitions are expected to strengthen its construction business, with the enlarged group projected to have a combined orderbook of about RM741.81 million upon completion.
The company said the larger orderbook and combined resources of GDB and the target companies would allow it to bid for larger and more complex construction projects, while improving economies of scale in the procurement of construction materials.
Separately, GDB plans to diversify into property development through its newly incorporated subsidiary, GDB Development Sdn Bhd.
The company said the property development business would provide an additional and recurring income stream to complement its existing construction operations.
It has acquired and identified potential land banks for a mixed-use development with an estimated gross development value of RM500 million, comprising serviced apartments, Soho units and retail components.
GDB said the diversification would help strengthen the company's resilience by broadening its earnings base and tapping alternative revenue streams.
The price for the construction companies was also supported by an independent valuation, which placed the fair value of their combined 51 per cent equity interests between RM76.04 million and RM88.70 million.
The acquisitions remain subject to, among others, shareholder and regulatory approvals, completion of due diligence and the successful completion of the private placement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends higher against Asean currencies, lower versus US dollar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher on Thursday against most Asean currencies, but lower against the US dollar amid a renewed surge in oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions in Middle East, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the ringgit inched down to 4.0890/0940 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0850/0895.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude rose 4.08 per cent to US$104.29 per barrel as the Middle East conflict is expected to be prolonged.
"In addition, concerns about fiscal sustainability in Europe, especially in France, have led to a stronger US dollar. It appears that … traders are seeking refuge against uncertainties," he told Bernama today.
At the close, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major currencies.
The local note went up against the British pound to 5.3930/3996 from 5.4049/4108 at Wednesday's close, strengthened against the euro to 4.5719/5775 from 4.5740/5790, but eased against the Japanese yen to 2.5834/5867 from 2.5797/5827.
The ringgit was traded mostly higher against its Asean peers.
The local note edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1893/1934 from 3.1919/1957 at Wednesday's close, and appreciated against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.51/6.52.
It appreciated against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.51/6.52, but weakened against the Thai baht to 12.1371/1563 from 12.1217/1386 previously.

Title: Haze turns Sun blazing red over Johor
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: The sun appeared blazing red over Johor today as haze blanketed the state, creating a striking sight across the skies.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the phenomenon was caused by the scattering of visible light by haze particles in the atmosphere.
"This is caused by the scattering of visible light due to the presence of haze in the atmosphere.
"It means tiny haze particles in the air bend and spread sunlight, making the Sun appear red or orange.
"It is common when the atmosphere is polluted.
"The reddish appearance is an optical effect caused by particles in polluted air altering the way sunlight travels through the atmosphere," he told the New Straits Times.
At 6pm today, all eight air quality monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Segamat recording the highest at 191.
This was followed by Kluang (180), Tangkak (175), Pasir Gudang (171), Larkin (170), Batu Pahat (165), Pengerang (157) and Kota Tinggi (154).

Title: 'Education, Health ministries must meet on measures for haze-forced school closures'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education and Health ministries need to meet immediately to find the best measures for school closures brought on by the haze enveloping the country.
The National Parent-Teacher Association said this follows the decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, that schools in areas where there was a prolonged spell of Air Polluntant Index readings of 150 and above to close.
Its president, Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohamad Ali Hasan, said the association respected the royal decree, which expresses concern for the safety and health of students as they face unhealthy air quality readings.
He said, prior to this, the guidelines were that school should close in areas of API readings of above 200, meaning at very unhealthy levels.
"When His Majesty advised the closure of schools in affected areas, particularly those recording an API reading of between 150 and 180 for a prolonged period, we need to take this into consideration for the safety and health of the students.
"Although this would conflict with the existing guidelines on school closures, in the association's view, perhaps schools could operate for only half a day if the reading reaches 150, whether during the morning or afternoon session, and close completely when the reading reaches 200.
"In any case, we will await further decisions from the Education and Health ministries," he said when contacted.
Ali said the safety and health of pupils and students must be prioritised, as haze can have adverse effects on health.
He said, when it comes to school closures, the Education and Health ministries need to make the final decision to ease parents' concerns.
"If a special advisory committee could be established to reach a consensus on the issue of school closures, that would actually be better.
"If there is no final decision, we could use both thresholds — API readings of 150 (partial closure) and 200 (full closure)."
Sultan Ibrahim, in a post on Facebook, had advised that
schools in affected areas
be closed, particularly those recording API levels between 150 and 180 for a prolonged period.
Expressing concern for the health and safety of schoolchildren, His Majesty decreed that the Education Ministry give serious attention to the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Haze: MoE institutions with API above 180 to shut from tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MoE) in areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 180 will be closed from tomorrow.
Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said this followed a decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, over pupils' safety and health amid the haze.
"All educational institutions under MoE in areas recording API readings above 180, based on readings recorded by the Department of Environment (DoE), must be closed from Friday.
"Educational institutions in areas where API readings remain above 150 for three consecutive days will close from this Monday.
"Affected schools and educational institutions under the ministry must implement home-based teaching and learning," he said in a statement.
Azam said schools must ensure lessons continue through suitable methods, taking into account pupils' capabilities, access and needs, as well as teachers' readiness.
Teachers and support staff would also be allowed to work from home throughout the closure period following the education minister's consideration.
He said state education departments, district education offices and institutions under the ministry must continuously monitor API readings and take appropriate action when the stipulated thresholds are exceeded.
The measures, Azam said, were aimed at protecting pupils and education personnel from exposure to haze that could affect their health.
Earlier, Sultan Ibrahim advised that schools in areas with prolonged
Air Pollutant Index (API) readings of between 150 and 180 be closed
amid the worsening haze.
In a statement on His Majesty's official Facebook page today, the King expressed concern over schoolchildren's health and safety and decreed that the Education Ministry give the matter serious attention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Exsim Hospitality bags RM15.6mil building works contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Exsim Hospitality Bhd's unit Exsim Concepto Sdn Bhd has clinched a RM15.62 million subcontract to supply and install building services and undertake general building works.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Exsim Hospitality said the subcontract works, awarded by Nestcon Builders Sdn Bhd, began today and are scheduled for completion on Oct 31, 2028.
The contract also carries a 27-month defects liability period from the date of the Certificate of Practical Completion.
Exsim Concepto is principally involved in specialised fit-out services for hospitality property assets, general contracting and centralised procurement.
Nestcon Builders is principally involved in construction works as well as providing licensed vehicle operator and transportation agent services.

Title: Viral park fight leads police to detain 13 students in Tawau
Article:
TAWAU: Police have detained 14 individuals, including 13 students, to assist in investigations into an armed brawl involving a group of teenagers at a park in Taman Ambar, Jalan Kuhara, here.
Tawau district police chief Assistant Commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said all those detained, aged between 12 and 14, were picked up by the Tawau police headquarters Criminal Investigation Department yesterday.
He said the 13 students were released on police bail, while a 14-year-old boy without identification documents was confirmed to be a non-student.
Police received a report on the incident at 6pm two days ago.
"Initial investigations revealed that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between two students before escalating into a fight involving several others.
"A viral video recording of the incident helped police identify the individuals involved and their respective roles in the incident," Rosdi said in a statement today.
He added that police seized a smartphone and a bicycle believed to be linked to the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for possessing weapons at a riot, while the undocumented teenager is also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Rosdi said further investigations were underway to determine the involvement and role of each individual detained.
"Police are obtaining the original video recording, recording statements from witnesses and the detainees, and securing the victim's medical report to complete the investigation.
"We are also collaborating with the school and the Tawau District Education Office regarding the incident," he said.
The fight went viral on social media in a 32-second video clip showing a group of teenagers in sports uniforms and secondary school attire pushing one another before several were seen scuffling, with one individual on the ground surrounded by others.

Title: Thailand starts extradition proceedings against Chinese journalist who exposed corruption
Article:
BANGKOK: Thai authorities began extradition proceedings on Thursday against a Chinese investigative reporter wanted by Beijing and detained for months in Thailand, his lawyer and an official told AFP.
Bai Zhaodong, 56, exposed government corruption in China over two decades before leaving in 2023 to escape "mounting persecution from the state", according to Reporters Without Borders (RSF).
Bai, who is recognised by the United Nations as a refugee, arrived in Thailand in 2024 and has been detained in the Southeast Asian country since January 2026, the media rights group says.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian said in July that Bai was suspected of extortion and bribery, and an extradition request had been submitted to Thailand.
"The prosecutor is bringing a case against him at court now. It is the beginning of the extradition hearing process," Prayuth Pecharakun, spokesman for Thailand's attorney general, told AFP on Thursday.
He said the process could take months.
Bai's lawyer Nadthasiri Bergman also confirmed to AFP that he had been taken to court to face extradition proceedings.
The hearing had not previously been made public, and RSF advocacy manager Aleksandra Bielakowska called the development "scandalous."
It came the day before an expected decision on a legal challenge brought by Bai's lawyers against Thai authorities over his continued detention.
"Bringing Bai Zhaodong before a court without notice, on the eve of a decision on the legality of his detention, is scandalous and shows how eager the Thai authorities are to bow to Beijing's demands," Bielakowska said.
RSF believes his life could be at risk if he is returned to China.
"We call on the international community to demand that Bangkok halt his deportation and allow him to travel safely to the country of his choice," Bielakowska said.
- 'RISKS TORTURE' -
Bai has been held at Bangkok's Suan Phlu immigration detention centre since Jan 21, according to the Southeast Asia Legal Defence Initiative, which represents him.
RSF has said that a third country has offered him asylum, without specifying which, but that departures planned for February and June were cancelled after Thai immigration authorities withheld exit clearance without explanation.
The media rights group and his lawyer have called on Thailand to grant the journalist permission to leave the country.
Beijing has long sought to clamp down on dissidents overseas, and campaigners accuse authorities in Thailand – where several notable activists have moved over the years – of complicity in China's efforts.
Thailand is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention, but is bound by the international legal principle of non-refoulement, which bars countries from sending people back to places where their lives or freedom are in danger.
Thailand's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to AFP's request for comment.
Nonetheless Bangkok deported 40 Uyghurs to China in February last year over the objections of activists, who said the men could be tortured or mistreated.
"For years, Bangkok has stepped up its cooperation with the Chinese authorities in their attempts to export their repression of journalism," the RSF's Bielakowska said.
She added: "Today, it is the Thai justice system that is paving the way for the handover of a journalist, recognised as a UN refugee, to a system where he risks torture, in breach of international law."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fatal highway crash: Trailer rams stalled car on NSE, triggering fire
Article:
MUAR: A 43-year-old man was killed after a trailer rammed a stalled car on the southbound stretch of the North-South Expressway early today.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the victim, a front passenger, died after the Proton Wira was struck by the trailer and dragged forward before bursting into flames.
The accident occurred at 12.15am at Km138.9.
"Initial investigations found that the car had broken down, and the driver and passengers stopped on the emergency lane.
"The vehicle's lights were not switched on. Shortly after, a trailer travelling from behind crashed into the rear of the car," he said in a statement today.
Raiz Mukhliz said the driver and another passenger managed to get out of the car before it was dragged forward by the impact and caught fire.
The 30-year-old driver suffered hand injuries and was taken to Muar Hospital, while the 43-year-old passenger suffered chest injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
An autopsy at Muar Hospital's forensic department found that the cause of death was multiple injuries consistent with a road traffic collision.
The 33-year-old trailer driver escaped injury, and urine and alcohol screening tests on him returned negative.
Raiz Mukhliz said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HI Mobility's unit to continue serving Johor Baru's residents with stage buses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HI Mobility Bhd's subsidiary, Handal Indah Sdn Bhd, has received a letter of intent (LOI) from the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) for its proposed appointment as the network operator under the stage bus service transformation (SBST) programme in Johor Baru.
The proposed appointment covers the period from Jan 1, 2027 to March 31, 2031.
In a statement, HI Mobility said the non-binding LOI allows Handal Indah to engage with APAD, an agency under the Transport Ministry, on its continued participation in the SBST programme.
It said the scope of services, contractual terms, contract value and other relevant matters would be developed and formalised before any letter of acceptance is issued.
The proposed appointment is in line with Handal Indah's expertise in smart mobility, fleet management and public transport operations.
The company said it would leverage technology, fleet capabilities and operational expertise to support a more efficient and reliable public transport network in Johor Baru and improve commuter connectivity.
HI Mobility executive director and chief executive officer Lim Chern Chuen said the company was encouraged by the LOI and the opportunity to build on Handal Indah's longstanding involvement in Johor Baru's public transport network.
"With Johor Baru continuing to strengthen its position as a major economic and connectivity hub, an efficient and well-connected public transport network will become increasingly important.
"We remain committed to working constructively with the government and relevant stakeholders to support Johor Baru's evolving mobility needs, and look forward to progressing discussions with APAD," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retiree loses RM70k to scammers posing as police
Article:
TANGKAK: A 68-year-old retiree lost RM70,000 after he was duped into handing over his ATM card to scammers posing as police officers.
The victim lodged a police report yesterday after discovering that seven cash withdrawals had been made from his account without his knowledge.
District police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said the victim was contacted by suspects who claimed he was involved in a money-laundering case.
"The suspects deceived the victim into handing over his ATM card by courier, claiming it was required by police for investigation purposes.
"The victim then found seven cash withdrawals were made without his knowledge, resulting in losses totalling RM70,000," he said in a statement today.
Roslan said the case was being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a maximum 10-year jail term, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

Title: Nestlé, Food Bank extend food aid partnership
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd and Yayasan Food Bank Malaysia (YFBM) have extended their food redistribution partnership for another three years, focusing on reducing food waste and supporting communities in need.
The collaboration, which began in 2020, was formalised through a new memorandum of understanding (MoU).
Nestlé Malaysia has contributed more than RM7 million worth of products through food redistribution and humanitarian relief initiatives carried out with YFBM to date.
As part of the latest collaboration, Nestlé employees and YFBM prepared 800 food and nutrition aid packs for families in remote areas of Tumpat and Jeli, Kelantan, ahead of the monsoon season.
The packs contain products including Milo, Everyday, Maggi, Nescafe, Nestum and Koko Krunch cereals.
The initiative forms part of Nestlé Malaysia's annual nationwide flood relief programme, which provides supplies to communities that may face difficulties accessing essential goods during prolonged heavy rain.
Under the new MoU, Nestlé Malaysia will continue to provide suitable surplus products, while YFBM will coordinate their safe distribution to beneficiaries.
Nestlé Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the partnership would allow surplus products to be redirected to communities that need them.
"With the monsoon season approaching, acting early is especially important for communities that may become harder to reach later in the year," he said.
YFBM chairman of the board of trustees YAM Tengku Zatashah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said consistent and organised food assistance was important in ensuring aid reached communities in need.
"Public-private partnerships such as this allow us to bring together food resources, volunteers and our distribution network to serve communities in need more effectively," she said.
The partnership also covers food redistribution and monsoon relief efforts targeting remote communities and isolated villages.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mustapha seeks higher Sabah, Sarawak development funds
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah and Sarawak Affairs Minister Datuk Mustapha Sakmud hopes the 2027 Budget will maintain or slightly increase development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak.
Sabah still needed substantial funding for basic infrastructure, particularly for recurring floods, road and water issues, he said.
"For the tabling of budget tomorrow, we hope that there will be good news for Sabah and Sarawak.
"As I have mentioned before, we want development funds, in particular, to either remain at the current level or be increased slightly," he told the media after handing over disaster relief aid to Sepanggar constituents at Kampung Rampayan community hall near here.
The Sepanggar MP also called for the Auditor-General's recommendations on the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway to be acted upon immediately and used to improve project management.
"I ask the Works Ministry, contractors and relevant agencies to increase their efforts to improve the effectiveness of project management.
"Take these audit recommendations positively and implement the findings. Let us use them as lessons so that similar problems do not recur in future projects," he said, referring to the decade-long project, which has recorded only 11 per cent completion.
Mustapha also hoped Phase 2 of the Kampung Rampayan flood mitigation project would be prioritised, saying he had discussed expediting the project with the Economy Minister.
He said the project, announced under Budget 2026, would continue Phase 1, which was almost completed, and help address recurring floods along the Rampayan River.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nurse stabbed 6 times by husband previously reported death threats to police
Article:
KOTA BARU: The 44-year-old nurse who was stabbed six times by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai near Kadok on Monday had lodged a police report in August after he had threatened to kill her.
A relative who declined to be named said the victim had been seeking a divorce after six years of marriage following repeated threats by her husband whenever they argued.
The relative said the victim lodged the report at the end of August and had since stopped living with the 47-year-old husband.
"She had been in the process of seeking a divorce as she could no longer tolerate the repeated threats," the relative said when met today.
He said the victim had previously lived in the Kampung Perol area but moved in with her mother in Padang Lepai near Ketereh about a month ago following a dispute with the suspect.
"The couple have a 3-year-old daughter, while the victim also has two children from her previous marriage," he added.
The victim, who works at Chempaka Health clinic, is currently receiving treatment at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital after suffering stab wounds to her body and neck.
The suspect surrendered at the Nilam Puri police station after the incident and was
remanded for seven days
until Oct 12.
The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a dangerous weapon which carries a jail sentence of up to 20 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Quarantine, unease and rumours: Russian city grapples with plague scare
Article:
WHEN a woman died of suspected plague in Siberia last week, Oksana was in the maternity ward for observation.
"Everything was fine, and then they told us that a woman had died. And they wouldn't let anyone in or out," the 35-year-old told AFP.
For four days, she was kept in hospital in Shelekhov, the same town where a 28-year-old lab worker, Darya Shipilova, had been hospitalised before she was reported to have died of plague.
Russian authorities have downplayed the incident, saying that she died from "pneumonia of an unknown aetiology" and that post-mortem analysis showed no trace of an infection connected with her "professional work" at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute.
Local media reports suggested she could have contracted the disease after breaking a test tube at the laboratory.
The incident has triggered global concern about a possible outbreak and calls for Russia to provide more information.
It has also drawn criticism and comparisons with Moscow's long history of downplaying or covering up the scale of health disasters – ranging from the Soviet response to the 1986 Chernobyl disaster to the coronavirus pandemic.
In Shelekhov, rumours have filled the information abyss.
"I've read about it being some kind of unclear pneumonia or Covid, something like that. To be honest, I don't believe in anything anymore," Oksana, who declined to give her surname, told AFP.
"There's so much information that I no longer know what to believe or who to listen to."
"The day it happened, my mum rang me, shouting that 10 people had already died, even though there were no official reports," Alexandra Iskalova, a 22-year-old who works in a medical centre, told AFP.
"I'd read somewhere that it was something like Hong Kong syphilis, and that it was actually caused by bears," she said, referring to a fictional disease from a popular Russian TV show.
"People were absolutely panicking because there were no official statements," she added.
On the streets, the town appears outwardly calm – no panic and few masks.
Yet many told AFP they are concerned.
"It's frightening," said Alina, 22.
"My brother's at primary school. They've already made masks compulsory, so they have to wear them everywhere. They're even allowed to stay off school if they're really worried."
[[nid:1550667]]
She said her aunt works at the anti-plague institute and was also quarantined.
Tatyana, 66, is also frustrated by the lack of official guidance from the authorities.
"Of course we're worried ... How on earth are we supposed to protect ourselves?"
"We don't know how the infection spreads. Or how it's detected," she added.
"There are a lot of rumours going around, all kinds of information, and it's unclear what's true. In reality, nobody is telling us what actually happened."
On Wednesday, World Health Organisation (WHO) chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged Moscow to clarify "media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause" from the Irkutsk institute.
When asked about a possible second case, the Kremlin appeared to reject it.
"The vast majority of what the media is reporting regarding this situation is false information," spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
Rospotrebnadzor said Wednesday that the situation in the Irkutsk region remained "stable", and that nearly 5,000 tests had been conducted, none of which revealed dangerous pathogens.
US President Donald Trump has offered to "help" Russia and said he would call his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to discuss the reports.
That offer was widely laughed off on the streets of Shelekhov.
"It's just funny," said Olga, a 68-year-old former accountant.
"In his heart he was probably happy that Russia had some problems, some kind of 'plague'," she added.
"He'd probably be glad if we really had an epidemic in our country."
* The article is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends lower amid higher oil prices, geopolitical risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower today, remaining under selling pressure ahead of 2027 Budget announcement tomorrow, as a renewed surge in oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia further dampened risk sentiment.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 10.77 points to 1,601.01 from Wednesday's close of 1,611.78.
The benchmark index opened 1.67 points higher at 1,613.45, marking its intraday high, and hit a low of 1,597.94 in the mid-morning session.
On the broader market, losers thumped gainers 813 to 378, while 482 counters were unchanged, 2,828 untraded and 13 suspended.
Turnover decreased to 3.51 billion units worth RM3.46 billion, compared with 3.83 billion units worth RM3.52 billion yesterday.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said Brent crude oil rose more than three per cent, driven by growing concerns over a potential escalation between the United States and Iran.
"For Malaysian equities, the combination of higher energy prices, geopolitical uncertainty and persistent foreign selling is becoming an increasingly important near-term headwind.
"Foreign investors have remained net sellers for 10 consecutive trading days as of yesterday, limiting the market's ability to absorb external shocks despite expectations surrounding 2027 Budget," it said.
He expects the FBM KLCI to remain volatile in the near term, with oil price movements, foreign fund flows and developments in US-Iran tensions likely to outweigh domestic catalysts ahead of 2027 Budget.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GEAR-uP to build Malaysia's capital pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's challenge is not simply making capital available, but ensuring it moves with businesses as they grow, industry observers said.
This will create opportunities for companies to scale, investors to participate and domestic capabilities to deepen.
They said promising startups have long faced difficulties securing successive rounds of financing.
Established businesses, meanwhile, often navigate a funding landscape that may not fully match their evolving needs.
Bridging these gaps requires more than individual funding programmes.
"This calls for a connected investment ecosystem where capital, expertise and institutional support work together," an observer said.
This is where the Government-linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP) could play a key role.
The programme seeks to connect different segments of Malaysia's investment landscape, spanning early-stage funding and venture capital to growth capital and, ultimately, the public market.
Industry observers said its most significant proposition is the commitment by six government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to deploy RM120 billion in additional domestic direct investments between 2024 and 2028.
However, they said GEAR-uP's longer-term value extends beyond the capital deployed.
Instead, the programme could help build a stronger pipeline of fund managers, investors and companies capable of scaling up and attracting capital over the longer term.
In 2025, RM2.6 billion was deployed through investment vehicles designed to bring private capital alongside government-linked funds.
This highlighted efforts to crowd in private investment and strengthen the domestic funding ecosystem.
CIMB Securities noted that GLICs deployed RM20.3 billion in domestic direct investments under the GEAR-uP programme in 2025.
This brought cumulative GEAR-uP investments over the past two years to RM26.9 billion, led by Khazanah Nasional Bhd with RM7.9 billion.
In 2024, the figure was RM6.6 billion.
Khazanah's Jelawang Capital has a RM1 billion mandate, while Kumpulan Wang Persaraan(Diperbadankan) (KWAP) established the RM500 million Dana Perintis.
Together, the initiatives channelled RM588 million into startups through selected fund managers.
KWAP's Dana Pemacu, meanwhile, deployed RM1.2 billion across 12 fund managers.
The significance of these initiatives goes beyond the capital reaching individual companies.
By backing local fund managers, GLICs are also helping them build expertise and track records that can support the growth of Malaysia's venture capital industry.
For Malaysian companies, this could mean greater access to experienced investors as they move from one stage of growth to the next.
When disclosing its latest report card recently, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan emphasised that GEAR-uP should be viewed beyond the amount of capital deployed.
Its wider objective is to catalyse additional investment, strengthen domestic capabilities and create sustainable economic opportunities.
While the RM20.3 billion refers to capital deployed by the institutions themselves, the wider aim is for this investment to encourage more private investors to participate alongside them.
"As the various funds and investments mature, it will be useful to look at how much private capital they attract, how companies perform and whether they go on to secure further funding and grow their businesses," the observer said.
These outcomes will take time, particularly for early-stage investments.
However, over the longer term, they will provide a clearer picture of how GEAR-uP is strengthening Malaysia's investment ecosystem.
Meanwhile, Dana Pemacu's 12 mandates also have the potential to develop greater expertise in sectors such as semiconductors, deep technology, energy transition, food security and the digital economy.
Building an investment ecosystem is not only about having more money available.
It is also about having investors with the expertise to identify promising businesses and support them as they grow.
The six participating GLICs collectively manage about RM2.2 trillion, giving them significant capacity to support domestic investment and develop local capabilities.
The RM1.2 billion placed with fund managers is strengthening the investment pipeline.
The RM588 million channelled into startups shows capital reaching companies at the earlier stages of their growth.
The next phase will be about how these investments develop over time - and how they bring more private investors, stronger fund managers and more Malaysian companies into the ecosystem.
If that cycle continues to strengthen, GEAR-uP can help give Malaysian companies greater access to capital while building a deeper pool of investment expertise in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Private jet operator CGT Asia denies wrongdoing, says four released after questioning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Private jet operator CGT Asia Limited has denied any wrongdoing after one of its aircraft was linked to an attempted trafficking of 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from Laos to the Philippines.
The company also confirmed that its director and three crew members, who were detained at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang yesterday, were released the same day after giving their statements to the Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID).
CGT Asia Limited's lawyer Kitson Foong said the company had never authorised the transportation of drugs or other illicit cargo.
He said all four who were detained had fully cooperated with investigators.
"The company's director and three members of its crew cooperated fully with NCID, gave statements and answered every question put to them to the best of their knowledge.
"All four were released on the same day they were detained," he said in a statement.
Foong said the aircraft which departed Subang for Luang Prabang, Laos, on Oct 1 had not been carrying any cargo when it left Malaysia.
He said the company had provided investigators with all relevant documentation concerning the flight, including details of those responsible for arranging it.
"As police have publicly confirmed, the aircraft departed Subang with no cargo on board.
"The company has placed before NCID all records and communications relating to the arrangement of the flight, including the particulars of the parties who arranged it," he said.
Foong said CGT Asia had never permitted its aircraft to be used to transport narcotics or other prohibited goods.
"The company does not carry and has never authorised or sanctioned the carriage of any narcotic, prohibited or illicit cargo.
"It maintains firmly that it has committed no wrongdoing," he said.
Foong also confirmed that two of the company's pilots remain in Laos following the drug seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1.
He said efforts were underway to secure their release and safe return.
"The company continues to support its two pilots in Laos.
"It is working with their families, their legal representatives and the relevant authorities towards their early release and safe return," he said.
Foong said CGT Asia's operations were continuing as usual in compliance with aviation regulations.
However, he said the company had introduced additional safeguards following the incident, including tighter due diligence and cargo verification procedures.
He said the measures took immediate effect and were aimed at ensuring that every flight met the highest standards of safety, security and integrity.
Foong added that the company's aircraft, flight crew and medical teams remained available to serve clients across the region.
He said the company would not comment further while investigations were ongoing.
Yesterday,
four people
including a pilot, co-pilot and two female crew members were detained at a hangar at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport shortly before their aircraft was scheduled to depart for Manila.
The operation followed the
seizure of 521kg
of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1.
Laos authorities detained 13 people in connection with the case, including a Malaysian aviation crew member.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Manufacturing firm fined RM30,000 over workplace accident, safety breaches
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: A manufacturing company was fined RM30,000 by the Sessions Court yesterday after a workplace accident left an employee with a permanent disability and exposed safety breaches.
The company was fined RM25,000 for failing to provide a safe operating system for a stamping machine, resulting in an accident involving a worker at 4pm on Jan 23.
The company was fined an additional RM2,500 each on two charges of failing to report the serious injury to the nearest Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) office immediately and failing to submit an accident report within seven days.
The sentence was handed down by Sessions Court Judge Roslan Hamid.
The charges were brought by Penang DOSH under Section 15(1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, punishable under Section 19 of the same Act, and Regulation 5(1)(b)(aa) and Regulation 5(1)(b)(bb) of the Occupational Safety and Health (Notification of Accident, Dangerous Occurrence, Occupational Poisoning and Occupational Disease) Regulations 2004.
"Employers have a legal responsibility to ensure the safety, health and welfare of workers, including providing safe work systems and identifying and controlling occupational safety and health risks," Penang DOSH said in a statement.
It reminded employers that workplace accidents must be reported according to legal requirements.
"The case serves as a reminder that failure to manage workplace safety and health risks could result in serious injuries, enforcement and prosecution.
"We will continue to intensify enforcement, inspections and advocacy efforts to ensure occupational safety and health remains a priority," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MISC secures 20-year charters for five new LNG carriers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MISC Bhd has secured long-term time charters for five newbuild liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers from Petronas LNG Ltd (PLL), with each vessel contracted for 20 years.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, MISC said it accepted a letter of award from PLL on Oct 7 for the long-term LNG shipping services.
"The project will be for a firm charter period of twenty years for each LNG carrier, with commencement expected in 2030. MISC will provide the LNG shipping services through its wholly owned subsidiaries," it said.
In connection with the project, MISC will enter into shipbuilding contracts with Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding (Group) Co Ltd for the construction of the five new LNG carriers.
MISC said the project would enable it to capitalise on Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) anticipated growth in LNG production while supporting the renewal of its LNG carrier fleet.
The new vessels are expected to improve fleet efficiency while helping to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and overall emissions intensity.
"The time charters include commercial, project execution and operational risks, inherent to the industry. MISC will take appropriate measures to mitigate these risks through established controls, experience and operational expertise," it added.
PLL is a Labuan-incorporated company principally involved in the buying and selling of LNG, the chartering of LNG vessels, and the transportation and supply of LNG.
It is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Petronas, which is also MISC's holding company.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMA: 63pc MO reporting rate in Sabah, Sarawak may not reflect ground staffing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called for greater transparency over the placement of medical officers (MOs) in Sabah and Sarawak, questioning whether the reporting rate has translated into more doctors on the ground.
MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan said the association had taken note of the Health Minister's announcement that about 63 per cent of MOs offered permanent placements in Sabah and Sarawak had reported for duty.
However, he said feedback from MMA's Sabah branch suggested the figures might not reflect the actual staffing situation at healthcare facilities.
"Several hospital departments are reportedly experiencing a net reduction in medical officers, while some doctors are having to undertake more on-call duties each month, including every-other-day (EOD) calls," he said in a statement.
He said public healthcare doctors could work continuously for 33 hours when placed on on-call duty.
"This raises an important question: Are the reported placements translating into an actual increase in doctors serving at healthcare facilities where they are most needed?" he said.
He called on the Health Ministry to clarify whether the reported figures included Sabah-born doctors, as well as MOs from Peninsular Malaysia who were already serving in Sabah and had chosen to remain there.
Sivanaesan also called for a detailed breakdown of MOs who had reported for duty following their permanent appointments, including those from Peninsular Malaysia and the specific public hospitals and health clinics in Sabah and Sarawak where they had been deployed.
He also sought the latest number of MOs from Peninsular Malaysia who had left Sabah to return to posts in the peninsula, as well as Sabah-born MOs who had left the state to take up positions in Peninsular Malaysia.
Sivanaesan also sought data on the net increase or decrease in MO staffing at individual hospitals and health clinics following the latest placement exercise.
He also reiterated MMA's call for a national healthcare workforce distribution dashboard with regularly updated data on the number, distribution and staffing gaps of healthcare personnel across public healthcare facilities nationwide.
"Such transparency is essential for identifying critical shortages, improving workforce planning and ensuring that healthcare resources are directed to where they are most needed," he said.
He explained that even with a 63 per cent reporting rate, more than one in three doctors offered placements had not reported for duty.
Addressing the manpower crisis in Sabah and Sarawak required more than placement exercises, with retention, better working conditions, fair allowances, adequate support and clear career development pathways also needed, he said.
"Ultimately, progress must be measured not merely by the number of doctors reporting for duty, but by whether healthcare facilities have sufficient manpower to deliver safe, timely and quality care to the rakyat," he said.
Earlier today, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said
about 63 per cent
of medical officers offered placements in Sabah and Sarawak reported for duty.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank sell-off casts pall in Southeast Asia, Singapore stocks drop 3pct
Article:
BENGALURU: Major banks in Southeast Asia declined more than one per cent on Thursday, with the region's top lender, DBS Group, dragging Singapore stocks more than three per cent lower as rising bond yields brought into focus risks to bank earnings growth and funding costs.
The MSCI EM Asia equities index declined 1.8 per cent in its worst day since early September, largely weighed down by a 2.6 per cent drop in South Korea's KOSPI.
In Singapore, the FTSE Straits Times Index shed as much as 3.2 per cent to hit its lowest since mid-July, with DBS dipping 5.2 per cent to mark its steepest daily loss since April last year. Smaller rivals OCBC and UOB fell nearly five per cent each.
Together, the three banks account for more than half of Singapore's main index, and make up more than a third of the MSCI Asean equity gauge, which marked its worst daily drop since early March.
JPMorgan and Citi raised concerns over Asean banks' earnings outlook, citing surging long-dated bond yields, higher funding costs and the normalisation of exceptional first-half wealth-related income.
"A combination of higher rates, AQ (asset quality) risks, funding tightness and capital-market-related revenue risks should impact quite a few bank stocks going into 3Q results," JPMorgan analysts led by Harsh Wardhan Modi wrote.
They recommend trimming exposure to all three major Singapore banks.
After a strong run in bank shares, investors may have become more sensitive to earnings risks and negative catalysts, said James Ooi, market strategist at Tiger Brokers.
"The market may also be reassessing the assumption that higher Singapore dollar interest rates are necessarily positive for banks. Higher rates can lift yields on loans and newly deployed assets, but they also push up what banks pay for deposits and other funding."
Singapore's central bank is expected to issue its quarterly monetary policy statement next week.
The negative sentiment crept into banking stocks across the region.
Malaysia's largest bank by assets Maybank fell as much as 0.6 per cent, pushing stocks in Kuala Lumpur down 0.9 per cent. Smaller rival CIMB Group slipped 1.9 per cent to hit its lowest in a year.
Thailand's Kasikornbank declined as much as 2.1 per cent to its lowest in three months.
South Korean stocks, meanwhile, dropped to a one-month closing low.
Samsung Electronics estimated a near ninefold jump in third-quarter earnings as booming demand for AI chips drove strong memory sales. The chipmaker's shares, however, slipped 2.4 per cent.
Tech-linked Taiwanese equities followed suit, slipping one per cent.
Most emerging Asian currencies traded in a tight range against a largely steady US dollar, with the exception of the Taiwan dollar depreciating 0.5 per cent.
An MSCI gauge of global emerging market currencies slipped marginally during Asia trading hours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drivers warned against high beams, hazard lights during haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Drivers have been advised against using high beams and hazard lights while driving in haze or thick fog, as reduced visibility can increase the risk of accidents.
The advice came from a coalition of road safety non-governmental organisations comprising the Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA), Malaysian Eminent Persons on Road Safety Forum Group (MEPORS) and Road Safety Alliance Malaysia (ROSAM), as part of a public service campaign.
The coalition said high beams could reflect off airborne particles during haze, creating glare and further reducing visibility.
"Drivers are advised to use low beams or fog lamps if visibility drops below 100 metres.
"Avoid turning on hazard lights while the vehicle is in motion, as this can confuse other road users and make it difficult for them to detect turn signals," it said.
The coalition also urged motorists to reduce their speed immediately when entering areas affected by dense smoke.
"On highways such as the North-South Expressway, where the standard speed limit is 110km/h, the recommended safe speed in thick haze is between 60 and 80km/h.
"At the same time, double the usual safe following distance from two seconds to at least four to six seconds," it said.
Road users were also advised to check live traffic conditions through navigation applications before starting their journeys and plan safer routes where necessary.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After 39 years, Sri Kumar prepares for life beyond the police force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: After nearly four decades of confronting armed criminals, protecting world leaders, training elite police commandos and managing national crises, Datuk M.V. Sri Kumar is preparing to hang up his uniform.
But for the veteran police officer, who officially retires on Sunday after more than 39 years of service, walking away from the force is not about having had enough.
Instead, it is about crossing the finish line of a career to which he has devoted almost his entire adult life.
"When you run a marathon, there has to be a finish line. When marathon runners see the finish line, they are excited. They don't say they want to run another 10km.
"In my line of duty, I want to cross that line having achieved what I have achieved.
"I survived the risks that came with the job and managed to maintain that momentum until the end. I can cross that line and say, I've done this," he told the
New Straits Times
in an exclusive interview ahead of his retirement ceremony tomorrow.
The Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director (crisis and disaster) said he remained physically and mentally capable of continuing his duties.
"I did what I loved. Therefore, it didn't feel like 39 years. Even now, I feel like I can continue because when you do something you love, it doesn't feel like work."
Sri Kumar's career began with the Police Field Force (now General Operations Force) in 1988, serving in jungle operations before an encounter during the 1989 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Kuala Lumpur changed his life.
Assigned to the Shangri-La Hotel, where then British prime minister Margaret Thatcher was staying, Sri Kumar spotted a group of armed men who looked unlike ordinary police personnel.
They were members of the elite Special Action Unit (UTK), then a largely clandestine unit whose operatives were rarely recognised by the public.
"When I saw this unit, I thought to myself, I think I belong here.
"At that time, people said the passing rate was only 10 per cent. Out of 100 people, only 10 would make it. I told myself, I am going to be among that 10 per cent."
After years of preparation, Sri Kumar underwent selection in 1992 at the age of 26, emerging as the top performer throughout the two-month physical training course.
Only 13 candidates successfully completed the programme.
He subsequently spent approximately 26 years with UTK, excluding a year at staff college, becoming its longest-serving training officer from 2000 to 2015.
During his time with the unit, Sri Kumar specialised in close protection, tactical operations and explosives.
His assignments included security details for prominent international figures, including former United States president Barack Obama, former vice-president Al Gore, former British prime minister John Major, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Philippine president Fidel Ramos.
"Close protection is one thing that I mastered. I also taught American special forces personnel close protection.
"They had very high regard for our training because it was not just academic. It was a practitioner teaching them."
While much of his operational history remains classified, Sri Kumar recalled participating in an operation against pirated video compact discs in which UTK personnel carried out an explosive entry to secure evidence.
Despite his extensive tactical experience, some of his greatest challenges came after leaving UTK in 2019.
As a senior officer in the Internal Security and Public Order Department, he helped coordinate police operations during the Covid-19 pandemic.
He was responsible for ensuring constantly changing movement control orders and standard operating procedures were communicated to police contingents nationwide.
"During Covid-19, we were the enforcers of the SOPs. We had meetings seven days a week, every day.
"Instructions from above had to go down, and issues from below had to come up."
The experience eventually led him into crisis and disaster management, where he trained district police chiefs in disaster response and critical thinking.
For Sri Kumar, the human element remains paramount.
"Artificial intelligence has no human touch or human feelings. The human brain is still needed.
"AI can tell you that you can place 5,000 people here and another 5,000 there. But it doesn't tell you about pregnant women, people with diabetes, cancer patients or children."
Sri Kumar cited the Putra Heights gas pipeline fire as an example of how crisis management required effective communication with victims.
He recalled explaining to people why firefighters could not immediately extinguish the flames and why residents were prohibited from returning to their homes.
"When people do not understand what is happening, they will create their own version of the story.
"The initial disaster had already happened. We had to make sure there were no further casualties."
Yet, of all his achievements, Sri Kumar said the legacy closest to his heart was the police Negotiation Cell.
Established some two years ago, the unit brings together personnel from several departments to handle crises involving hostages, kidnappings and other emergencies.
As its commander, Sri Kumar helped develop the unit's training framework and operational guidelines.
His efforts culminated in the launch of the police
Negotiators Guidelines Book
by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail at Bukit Aman on Monday.
[[nid:1550631]]
"This book is the brainchild of all of us. Everyone had a portfolio and a subject to master.
"We produced something that will remain even after I leave. The knowledge must not fade away."
Sri Kumar also designed the unit's crest, featuring a horse which symbolises strength and negotiation, a shield representing protection and a handshake signifying peaceful resolution.
"There is no rifle or gun in the crest. At the end of the negotiation, what we want is a handshake."
Beyond the book, Sri Kumar hopes his greatest contribution will be the younger officers he has mentored.
"You have to be approachable. I treat them as family. I want to create future leaders. They should not have to wait 40 years to gain the experience I have."
Away from his professional achievements, Sri Kumar credited his late mother for instilling the values that guided his career.
His father died when he was just 7, leaving his mother to raise four children.
"What made me who I am today was my mother's upbringing. When you have stars on your shoulders, remember that your mother is watching. So do the right thing."
Sri Kumar said integrity, discipline, professional excellence, family and health were the five principles he lived by.
As retirement approaches, Sri Kumar intends to spend more time with his wife of 25 years and their two sons, beginning with a holiday in November.
He also plans to continue mentoring the Negotiation Cell.
"You have to accept that this era of your life is done and embrace the next chapter. I don't know exactly what it will look like, but I have to embrace it."
For the veteran officer, retirement is not an admission that he can no longer serve, but the satisfaction of completing his journey on his own terms.
"I still have the physical and mental ability to continue. But when you see the finish line, you want to cross it."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTS Link construction unaffected by Anthony Loke resignation
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Construction of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link will proceed as scheduled despite Transport Minister Anthony Loke's decision to resign from the Cabinet.
Loke said his resignation had no bearing on the cross-border project, with physical works and technical preparations continuing under the contractors and appointed operators.
"This has nothing to do with my resignation. The work will continue as usual. For the RTS Link, all tasks are being handled by the contractors and the teams on the ground.
"At ministry level, we make policy decisions and act as the project's spokesperson, but this will not affect the project's progress according to the established timeline," he said at a press conference after launching the BAS.MY Johor Baru service expansion at JB Sentral today.
Also present was Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
Loke said on Sept 29 that he had
submitted his resignation
as a Cabinet minister to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
However, he was
asked to remain
as transport minister for an agreed period until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returned home.
Loke offered to resign following an emergency DAP Central Executive Committee meeting in protest against the decision involving Najib's house arrest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan 2027 Budget to be tabled on Nov 27, says MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan state government will convene the state legislative assembly on Nov 26, followed by the tabling of the state's 2027 Budget on Nov 27, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
He said the sitting scheduled for Oct 16 would be postponed to the end of November.
Ismail said the absence of state executive councillors (Exco) would not affect preparations for the budget, as the state government could make decisions on the budget without the Exco.
"It can be tabled. Usually, we bring the budget to the Exco for approval, but it is not mandatory.
"Under normal circumstances, the budget prepared by the departments can also be brought directly to the assembly," he told reporters after the briefing and appointment letter presentation ceremony for the Negeri Sembilan Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) 2026-2028 term.
Ismail said the state government would consult all 25 government assemblymen on the budget this month, adding that the views of all elected representatives would be taken into account in its preparation.
"We are postponing it until the end of November so that the opening of the assembly sitting and the Budget can be held together.
"The postponement is because there was not enough time. What matters now is the Budget. What we need to do for the state and the people is the Budget," he said.
In his speech earlier, Ismail acknowledged that the ongoing turmoil in the state had sparked various controversies and questions among the public, both in Negri Sembilan and nationwide.
The Jusseh assemblyman said he would continue to discharge his duties as menteri besar to the best of his ability, while ensuring the state administration continued to function as usual and the interests of the people remained the priority.
"Despite the various challenges, as menteri besar, I will continue to shoulder this responsibility and will not waver in my duty to safeguard the interests of the people and ensure Negri Sembilan continues to move forward.
"I want the people of Negri Sembilan to remain confident and calm. We will not allow the current turmoil to disrupt their lives.
"The government must continue working, development must continue and the people must continue to be cared for," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nhaveen murder trial: Accused admits taunting victim, denies assault
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Two of four men accused of murdering bullying victim T. Nhaveen nine years ago told the High Court today that they only taunted him at a burger stall on the night of the incident.
First accused J. Ragesuthen, 27, in his written statement before judge Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid, said he and co-accused K. Tatisan, 26, were buying burgers in Taman Tun Sardon when they encountered Nhaveen, then 18, and T. Previin, then 19.
"I saw Previin and Nhaveen at the burger stall. Tatisan and I taunted Nhaveen, but I cannot recall what was said. After that, Tatisan and I went to our usual hangout spot to meet Gokulan and Sharmah," Ragesuthen said during defence proceedings.
Ragesuthen, Tatisan, S. Gokulan, 27, and V. Sharmah, 27, were called to enter their defence for murdering Nhaveen and causing grievous hurt to Previin near the Karpal Singh Learning Centre in Jalan Kaki Bukit, Gelugor, between 11pm and midnight on June 9, 2017.
Ragesuthen testified that while at Jalan Kaki Bukit, Previin and Nhaveen arrived on a motorcycle and asked Tatisan why he was taunting Nhaveen, before Previin allegedly struck Tatisan with a helmet.
"During the scuffle, Gokulan and Sharmah came to break up the fight. I saw Previin hit Sharmah with a helmet, causing Sharmah to lose consciousness," he said.
He said another man known as "Belang" intervened and took Nhaveen away on his motorcycle, while Previin left on his own machine.
"Tatisan, Gokulan, and I helped send Sharmah home for medical treatment. After that, I did not know what happened to Previin, Belang, and Nhaveen," Ragesuthen said.
Under cross-examination by deputy public prosecutor Mohd Amril Johari, Ragesuthen repeatedly denied that he and the three other accused beat Nhaveen, causing his injuries and death.
Amril put it to Ragesuthen that he and Tatisan had taunted Nhaveen by calling him a derogatory name, which the accused denied.
Ragesuthen admitted that this was the first time in court he claimed Sharmah was struck by Previin and knocked unconscious, but disagreed with the prosecution's assertion that the accused four had instead attacked Previin and Nhaveen.
He denied 'locking' Previin's neck while Tatisan hit him and threw him into a drain, and rejected suggestions that they continued attacking Nhaveen with helmets at Padang Openg despite the victim begging them to stop.
Ragesuthen also denied receiving a phone call from Nhaveen's mother, Shanti, or telling her that they would not send Nhaveen back until the matter was settled.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US ambassador to Greece sought US$100,000 from donor: WSJ
Article:
ATHENS: The United States' Ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, sought US$100,000 from a donor and offered access to top administration officials, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
Several Democrats have accused Guilfoyle – a former fiancee of President Donald Trump's son, Donald Jr – of promoting the commercial interests of a Greek company during official engagements and called on the US State Department to review her conduct.
Guilfoyle offered to use her sway to help Trump donor Eric Deters on tax and legal issues, and asked him to pay a US$100,000 bill she owed American Express, according to the Journal.
"It won't show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express. Please," she reportedly said in Signal messages to Deters.
"Honey please I need you to get this done for me today," she wrote in July 2025, days before the confirmation hearing for her ambassadorship, according to screenshots posted by the Journal.
Deters said he did not make the payment. A lawyer for Guilfoyle told the Journal that the ambassador disputed the authenticity of the messages.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on the article on Thursday.
Rubio was in Athens to participate in a "strategic dialogue" with Nato member Greece on regional and energy security, as part of a European tour.
A US Embassy official told the Journal that "Guilfoyle's career in and out of public service is guided by deep and abiding values."
"She was fully vetted by the bipartisan Senate Foreign Relations committee and confirmed by the US Senate. The Ambassador remains committed to representing the American people with dedication and integrity," the official said.
Deters, the Trump donor, said his dealings with Guilfoyle began in 2020 but she "never came through" on favours promised to him.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MyDCD signs underwriting agreement with TA Securities ahead of ACE Market listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MyDCD Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with TA Securities Holdings Bhd ahead of its proposed listing on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market.
The company is undertaking an initial public offering (IPO) comprising 335 million new ordinary shares and an offer for sale of 145 million existing shares.
Of the 335 million new shares, 89.7 million will be offered to the Malaysian public through balloting, while 36 million will be made available to eligible directors, employees and persons who have contributed to the success of MyDCD and its subsidiary.
Another 50.71 million shares will be offered to selected investors through private placement, with the remaining 158.59 million shares allocated to selected Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
The 145 million existing shares under the offer for sale comprise 79.34 million shares for selected investors and 65.66 million shares for selected Bumiputera investors approved by the ministry, both through private placement.
TA Securities will underwrite the 89.7 million public issue shares offered to Malaysian investors through balloting.
MyDCD, through its wholly owned subsidiary DCD Technology Sdn Bhd, specialises in the integration of mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection systems and subsystems for critical infrastructure, particularly data centres.
Its services cover engineering support, supply and installation, testing and commissioning, as well as corrective and preventive maintenance.
The company serves various players across the data centre ecosystem, including operators, telecommunications companies, information and communications technology service providers, financial institutions, government bodies, and property and investment companies.
Its project track record includes work for Bursa Malaysia, MEC Jati Consortium Sdn Bhd for a data centre owned by Telekom Malaysia Bhd, Nakano Construction Sdn Bhd for a Tier III data centre, Petronas group of companies and Binastra Builders Bhd.
From financial year 2023 (FY23) to FY25, MyDCD completed MEPF system and subsystem integration projects for data centres with a total project value of RM549.30 million.
For FY25, the company recorded revenue of RM371.98 million, equivalent to about four per cent of Malaysia's MEPF market, according to its independent market research report.
MyDCD said it has experience across enterprise, colocation and hyperscale data centres, covering Tier I to Tier IV environments.
The company also holds the relevant approvals, licences, certificates and permits for its operations, including registrations with the Construction Industry Development Board, Finance Ministry and Energy Commission, as well as contractor registration with Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
It also has authorised partnerships with technology and equipment providers including Huawei, Riello UPS and Vertiv.
Proceeds from the IPO will mainly be used for working capital and business expansion, including hiring additional staff for its project, engineering and human resources departments, renting new office space and staff training.
Part of the proceeds will also be used to enhance its information technology systems and defray listing expenses.
MyDCD chief executive officer Chris Ow Yong said the company was looking to scale up as Malaysia strengthens its position as a regional data centre hub.
"Having been involved in Malaysia's data centre MEPF industry for about 15 years, we have seen the market evolve from the early development of data centre infrastructure to the emergence of Malaysia as an increasingly important regional data centre hub," he said.
He said factors such as cost competitiveness, reliable utilities and policy support had supported Malaysia's growth as a data centre location, with Johor also benefiting from lower operating costs and proximity to Singapore.
The company expects Malaysia's data centre market to grow from US$4.04 billion in 2024 to US$13.57 billion by 2030.
Ow Yong said the IPO would provide MyDCD with resources to strengthen its project and engineering capabilities, expand its workforce and enhance its operational infrastructure.
TA Securities head of corporate finance Ku Mun Fong said MyDCD's track record and specialised MEPF expertise positioned it to benefit from rising demand for data centre infrastructure in Malaysia.
MyDCD is expected to be listed on the ACE Market in the fourth quarter of 2026.
TA Securities is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ‘Tonto’ pleads not guilty to 55 bribery charges totalling RM62,900 involving traffic police
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — A ‘tonto’ (lookout) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to 55 charges of giving RM62,900 in bribes to three traffic police officers between January 2022 and February 2026.
Ang Lie Giap, 33, entered the plea after all the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin.
According to the charges, the man was alleged to have corruptly given money to three traffic police officers from the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters, Negeri Sembilan Contingent Police Headquarters and the Kesas Expressway EMPV Patrol Office, as an inducement for them not to inspect lorries during roadblocks.
The bribes were allegedly given in several transactions at several bank branches in Klang and Setia Alam, involving amounts ranging from RM700 to RM2,000.
In a separate case, a logistics manager of a company, R Yuvarajakumar, 42, also pleaded not guilty at the same court to 16 charges of giving RM4,200 in bribes to a Road Transport Department (JPJ) enforcement assistant between May 2023 and October 2024.
According to the charges, the father of two was alleged to have corruptly given money to an enforcement assistant at JPJ Wangsa Maju through several transactions into several bank accounts belonging to a woman at a bank branch in Sungai Buloh, as an inducement for the officer not to inspect lorries.
All the offences were allegedly committed under Section 17(b) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for imprisonment for up to 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The prosecution in both cases was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Asmaa’ Zamri.
Earlier, Asmaa’ offered bail of RM15,000 for Ang and RM10,000 for Yuvarajakumar, with one surety each, together with additional conditions that the accused report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office once a month, surrender their passports and not interfere with prosecution witnesses.
However, lawyer K Theivaendran, representing Ang, applied for the bail to be reduced to RM10,000 and for his passport not to be surrendered to the court, as his client needed to travel abroad frequently for religious matters. He also informed the court that the accused’s wife was pregnant and expected to deliver their first child today.
“The accused is not a flight risk and works helping to manage his father’s chicken farm business, earning between RM3,000 and RM3,500 a month,” said the lawyer, who appeared together with lawyers Varghese Onny, Tee Yuan Sheng and Tee Kar Weng (PDK).
Lawyer Datuk Dr Aswandi Mohamed Hashim, representing Yuvarajakumar, meanwhile applied for the bail to be reduced to RM5,000, saying it was his client’s first offence and that he needed to support his mother, who suffers from asthma.
The court subsequently allowed Ang and Yuvarajakumar to be released on bail of RM15,000 and RM5,000 respectively, with one surety each, and ordered them to report to the MACC office once a month and not interfere with witnesses. Yuvarajakumar was also required to surrender his passport.
The court set Dec 3 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Myanmar agree ministries must act together on refugee cooperation, says PM Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Myanmar agree that relevant ministries and agencies need to take coordinated and proactive action to advance bilateral cooperation, including efforts to address the issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was emphasised during his meeting and bilateral talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today.
He said following their joint press conference, he and Min Aung Hlaing attended the Malaysia-Myanmar Cooperation Dialogue at Kompleks Seri Perdana, organised by the Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia.
He said the dialogue complemented efforts to strengthen understanding between Malaysia and Myanmar through the participation of academics, scholars, think tanks and business communities from both countries.
“I stressed that everything discussed during the one-to-one meeting and bilateral talks must be followed up with concrete action,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said the government supported the dialogue initiative and encouraged broader participation by academic institutions and the business community so that the discussions could be translated into cooperation that directly benefited the people.
“I believe open dialogue and committed follow-up will strengthen trust between Malaysia and Myanmar, while paving the way to resolve outstanding issues and expand cooperation that brings tangible benefits to Malaysians,” he said.
Min Aung Hlaing departed for home today after concluding his two-day official visit to Malaysia, which began yesterday. — Bernama

Title: NRD issues 169,346 new generation MyKads nationwide in three weeks
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 8 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has issued a total of 169,346 New Generation MyKads nationwide between September 17 and October 6.
NRD Director-General Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias said the five states recording the highest issuance are the Federal Territories with 20,592 pieces; Johor (18,871); Sarawak (15,777); Sabah (13,711) and Selangor (13,452).
He said that so far, the response received from the public has been very encouraging due to the upgrade from 23 to 53 high-tech security features capable of curbing identity forgery issues.
“To accommodate the increase in applications for the New Generation MyKad, the NRD has increased card production centres from 60 to 70 nationwide. Only one is not yet operational, which is in the Langkawi district. However, it is in its final preparation stage and is expected to operate soon.
“Based on NRD records for the month of September, male applicants recorded a higher application percentage at 57 percent compared to females. However, we would like to advise the public not to rush to change their old MyKads to the new generation if the chip is still in good condition,” he said after the Mekar Komuniti programme at Taman Sinar Harapan, here today.
Also present was Terengganu NRD Director Awatif Hannan Md Yusup.
Badrul Hisham said 25 Mekar programmes have been implemented in Terengganu this year to facilitate the public, including persons with disabilities (OKU), Orang Asli, chronic patients, mental patients, and senior citizens in obtaining their MyKads.
He said these figures are not just achievement statistics, but rather depict the lives of the people touched through NRD services.
“In addition, the Terengganu NRD has also provided 1,314 advisory service sessions to the community this year. Behind a single piece of MyKad, there is a name, a life, an identity, dignity, and a human being.
“The NRD’s task is not just to manage identity cards, but to safeguard the people’s identity and the nation’s trust. We want an NRD that is not only efficient in its systems, but has heart in its services,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anthony Loke: RTS Link not delayed, buffer time needed for safety approvals
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Singapore jointly decided to start the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link operations in February 2027, rather than taking a unilateral step, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said the project was not delayed. Instead, additional time was needed to allow an independent safety consultant to conduct a final evaluation and to secure technical approvals from authorities in both countries.
The minister said the approvals involved Malaysia’s Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) and Singapore’s Land Transport Authority (LTA).
“After taking these considerations into account, both parties, through the operator RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO), informed their respective authorities.
“I have also communicated with Singapore’s Transport Minister, and we agreed that the best decision is to commence operations in February so that all processes can be executed as thoroughly as possible,” he told a press conference after launching the BAS.MY service expansion at Johor Bahru Sentral here today.
He said RTS Link operations could start as early as January, but February was chosen to provide a buffer and ensure safety evaluation and technical approvals proceed smoothly.
