He added that physical work on the RTS Link station and the Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex building was complete, while October to December was a critical phase for testing and commissioning before the system was handed over to the operator by Dec 31.
Loke explained the government does not want to risk rushing the process, as the RTS Link is a cross-border project involving safety and will serve thousands of passengers daily.
He said February is a comfortable timeframe for both nations to complete testing, safety evaluations, and technical approvals.
Loke said the opening date will be announced only after APAD and LTA grant all approvals, and the government remains confident the service will start in February 2027.
Previously, RTSO said that all system testing and trial runs are targeted for completion by Dec 31 this year, with passenger services expected to start in February 2027, compared to the initial expectation of operations commencing in January. — Bernama

Title: SUV driver fined RM4,000 for tailing Zahid Hamidi’s police convoy on Kesas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A property agent was fined RM4,000 by the Magistrates’ Court here today after pleading guilty to disobeying a police order by following the convoy escorting Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday.
Magistrate Nurul Izzah Hasan Basri imposed the fine on Bryan Marc Daniel, 27, and ordered him to serve eight months in prison if he failed to pay the fine. He subsequently paid the fine.
According to the charge, the accused, who was driving a sports utility vehicle (SUV), disobeyed a police officer’s order while the officer was carrying out his duties on the Shah Alam Expressway (KESAS), from Kajang towards Subang Jaya, at 9.32am yesterday.
The offence was charged under Section 21(2) of the Police Act 1967, which provides for a fine of up to RM10,000 or imprisonment for up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
The case was handled by Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Farhanah Arul Hisham, while lawyer R. Karnan represented the accused.
Earlier, a video went viral showing an SUV driver following a police convoy escorting the Deputy Prime Minister from Kajang towards Sunway Medical Centre in Subang Jaya.
In the video, a police escorting officer warned the driver not to follow the convoy, but the man refused to comply and continued to do so. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia must strengthen regional cooperation to ensure stable energy supply, says Akmal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia has highlighted the need to strengthen regional cooperation to ensure a stable and affordable energy supply, alongside efforts to accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, representing the Malaysian government, conveyed this position at the 4th Asia Zero Emission Community (Azec) Ministerial Meeting in Manila, the Philippines today.
In a statement, the Ministry of Economy said that the Azec collaboration complements the implementation of the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), including energy efficiency, renewable energy, green mobility, infrastructure development, and transition financing.
“Malaysia also sees opportunities for cooperation in methane emission reduction, hydrogen, and carbon capture, utilisation, and storage (CCUS) technologies.
“Malaysia welcomes support from Japan and Azec partners in the areas of technology, financing, and capacity building,” the statement said.
During the discussion, Akmal Nasrullah highlighted that a just energy transition must consider people’s needs, the country’s own capacity, and economic growth.
All 11 Azec member countries attended the meeting: Japan, Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.
The meeting was co-chaired by the Japanese Economy, Trade and Industry Minister’s representative Takagi Kei and Philippine Energy Secretary Sharon S Garin.
The discussion focused on the resilience of energy supply amidst geopolitical uncertainty, including the risk of supply route disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.
The members also discussed efforts to voluntarily increase oil storage capacity — subject to their respective circumstances and capabilities — as well as cooperation under the Japan-led Powerr (Partnership On Wide Energy and Resources Resilience) Asia initiative on energy security.
Earlier, Akmal Nasrullah also held a bilateral meeting with Josh Wilson, the Deputy Climate Change and Energy Minister from Australia’s Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, focusing on energy supply security and gas supply between the two countries.
Bilateral discussions were also held with Takagi, covering Malaysia’s role in Azec and opportunities for cooperation in CCUS and hydrogen.
The session continued with a special meeting involving Middle Eastern oil-producing nations, namely Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, to discuss opportunities for collaboration on strategies to ensure security of petroleum supply.
Akmal Nasrullah also witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding between IHI Corporation and TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd for a feasibility study on ammonia fuel development, as well as the exchange of a letter of intent between Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (Meti) and the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) regarding energy transition. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan warns: Dogs without anti‑rabies vaccination tags may be culled
Article:
BACHOK, Oct 8 — Dogs without vaccination tags or that have not received anti-rabies vaccinations after April each year may be culled by local authorities in Kelantan to curb the risk of rabies transmission.
State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the provision is in line with the Kelantan Anti-rabies Vaccination Order, which requires owners to ensure their pet dogs are vaccinated between January and April every year.
He said every vaccinated dog would be issued a numbered metal identification tag before being licensed by the local council, and animals without the tag or that have not been vaccinated after April could face action.
“Under the order, all dog owners are required to ensure their pets receive vaccinations between January and April every year to prevent the spread of rabies,” he said in a press conference after officiating the Peatland Fire Prevention programme hands-on standard operating procedure (SOP) training at Kampung Kual Besar, Gunong here today.
Hilmi said Kelantan, which borders Thailand, also faces the risk of rabies transmission due to the possibility of dogs moving across the border between the two countries.
He said a rabies-related death reported in Kubang Pasu, Kedah, last month, as well as the stray dog attack involving a child in Kelantan early this month, served as a reminder of the dangers of the disease, which can be fatal.
He said the local councils, in collaboration with the Department of Veterinary Services also conducted periodic operations to catch stray dogs, with two of the five dogs identified so far having been caught and culled.
“This year, 21 dogs in Bachok have been vaccinated, while samples from another 20 dogs have been taken for rabies testing,” he said.
As such, Hilmi urged all dog owners to ensure that their pets are vaccinated, licensed with the local council and not allowed to roam freely to ensure public safety. — Bernama

Title: Three Pontian siblings killed in motorcycle‑lorry crash after insisting on school despite haze closure
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 8 — Unconvinced that the school had been closed due to the haze today, an elder brother eventually gave in to his two younger siblings’ insistence on going to school on a motorcycle, before all three were killed in an accident at Jalan Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong, here, this morning.
The victims’ mother, Julaiha Munaji, 44, said that her two children, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha, eight, still wanted to go to Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Sapran, despite being informed that the school had been closed due to the haze.
She said that they did not believe that the school had been closed, with one of them even reportedly pleading to go to school, while wearing their school uniform and preparing their schoolwork.
As a result, their 18-year-old brother, Nor Daniel Aiman, eventually took both siblings to school on a motorcycle before they were involved in an accident with a lorry about 200 metres from their family home.
“I was informed by villagers that my children had been involved in an accident, but at first I thought it was an ordinary accident. I then told my eldest son, Nor Daniel Irwan, 22, to go to the location.
“When Irwan returned, he was crying and told me that Fikri and Naufa had died, while Aiman was in critical condition.
“I felt as though I was going to faint when I heard the news. I could only recite istighfar, and tears streamed down my face without me realising it,” she told Bernama at her home in Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, here, today.
Julaiha said that a day before the incident, Nor Daniel Fikri, her fifth child, had washed his football boots, as he was due to attend football training today, in preparation for an upcoming competition in which he was to represent his school.
She added that her son was very passionate about football and aspired to go further in the sport.
“He did not want to miss the training and had already put on his sports attire this morning. Aiman, meanwhile, was supposed to further his studies at GiatMARA, but his plans did not materialise, as he died while on the way to the hospital,” she said.
Earlier, Pontian police chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain, in a statement, said that the accident, which occurred at about 7.20am, involved a Honda motorcycle ridden by an 18-year-old man with two pillion riders, aged 11 and eight, and a Hino lorry.
He said the motorcycle was travelling from Jalan Parit Haji Omar towards Kayu Ara Pasong, before it was believed to have collided with the lorry travelling in the opposite direction, with the two pillion riders pronounced dead at the scene, while the motorcycle rider died on the way to Pontian Hospital.
All schools in Johor have been closed for two days, from today, following the deterioration in air quality in the state, affecting more than 1,000 schools and about 600,000 students. — Bernama

Title: Steven Sim: Tourism surge and foreign fans drive RM345m SME gains from Bahrain F1 GP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) reaped over RM345 million in economic spillover effects of the Bahrain Gulf Air Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix (GP) at Sepang International Circuit.
Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong added that almost half of the 261,000 spectators were foreign tourists.
“The impact reflects the important role of large-scale international sporting events in stimulating economic activities, especially through the rise in tourism expenditure and demand for local goods and services.
“The Bahrain F1 GP in Malaysia has had a very drastic impact on the SMEs, especially those in the hospitality, food and beverage, retail, transport, entertainment, tourism-related services and support industries,” he said in a statement today.
Those who attended the F1 race were projected to have spent 2.17 times more than ordinary events, he said, adding that foreign tourists usually spend more due to longer stays and expenditure spent for accommodation, food and beverages, transport, shopping and recreational activities.
Based on the success and economic spillover effect, Malaysia could benefit from international sporting events such as the G1 as a platform for SMEs to have wider opportunities and market access.
“This effort includes strengthening ties between SMEs and bigger industry players, event organisers, tourism operators and local suppliers so that the economic benefits generated by such large-scale events can be enjoyed by more small businesses,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Dzulkefly: Food Bill proposes publishing non-compliant food information without court order
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government has proposed expanding the powers of the Director-General of Health to publish information on food that does not comply with the Food Act 1983 (Act 281) or regulations made under it, without a court order.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal under the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 would allow such information to be published through print or electronic media in the interest of public safety.
“The existing provisions under Act 281 are no longer adequate to address current food safety challenges and protect public health,” he said when tabling the bill for second reading in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said the 39-clause bill also proposed amendments to Section 12 of Act 281 to allow convictions under the act to be published through print or electronic media.
In addition, he said a new Section 11A was proposed to expand the powers of the Director-General of Health to close premises that prepare or sell food containing substances injurious to health.
Dzulkefly said the amendments would also strengthen enforcement by expanding the powers of authorised officers to conduct investigations, in addition to their existing inspection powers.
He said the officers would also be given access to recorded information, computerised data and digital data to enable thorough investigations to be conducted in line with the development of transactions made online.
He added the amendments would also empower officers to obtain information on food advertising and inspect books, documents or records at relevant premises, including premises involved in producing food advertisements.
On consumer safety, Dzulkefly said the bill would strengthen controls over food contact materials, including making it an offence to prepare or sell materials that contain, or can transfer, poisonous or hazardous substances.
“Operators will also be required to immediately recall, remove or withdraw from sale any food contact materials if they know or have reason to believe that the materials contravene the provisions of Act 281,” he said.
He said the government proposed increasing the fines and maximum prison terms, including a penalty of up to RM25,000 or imprisonment for a maximum of five years, or both, for offences against regulations made under the act.
To strengthen controls on imported food, he said the bill proposed that food brought into Malaysia by land, sea or air in excess of the prescribed limit be deemed to be intended for sale unless proven otherwise.
Dzulkefly said on-site verification of overseas food facilities could also be carried out following prior consultation with the exporting country to ensure that only safe imported food is allowed to enter Malaysia.
Meanwhile, he said the food safety challenges faced by the government included chemical contamination caused by the misuse of pesticide and antibiotic residues, excessive use of food additives, as well as the emergence of new chemicals and pathogens.
He said Act 281 had never undergone a comprehensive review since it was gazetted in 1983, although it had been amended three times, in 2001, 2006 and 2024, involving specific provisions and consequential amendments arising from the enactment of other laws.
He added that engagement sessions with various stakeholders had been held from 2023 to 2026, in addition to public consultations and notification to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to obtain feedback on the proposed amendments. — Bernama

Title: AGC objects to former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez’s bid to challenge IRB over RM4.8m tax settlement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has objected to former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings against the Inland Revenue Board (IRB), over its alleged unilateral cancellation of an agreement on the settlement of RM4.8 million in tax and penalties.
Senior Federal Counsel (SFC) Ng Siew Wee said the application was premature as the impugned letter issued by the IRB to the former Baling MP on August 7 stated that a new tax computation would be issued in due course and did not raise a fresh assessment or demand payment of any quantified sum.
Ng said the impugned letter stated that a review of the case had uncovered new findings and facts concerning income allegedly omitted from the agreement, resulting in the cancellation of the agreement and consequently, the composite assessment with a new tax computation to be issued in due course.
“Abdul Azeez was not directed by the impugned letter to pay any additional tax. No amount of additional tax was determined. No fresh assessment had been issued at the time the present application was commenced,” she said during the hearing of the leave application by Abdul Azeez before Judge S Indra Nehru at the High Court here, today.
Lawyers Nicholas Mark Pereira, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad and Tan Sri Dzulkifli Ahmad appeared for Abdul Azeez, while SFC Ng appeared for the AGC, together with IRB Senior Revenue Counsel Marina Ibrahim.
In his application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings filed on September 6, Abdul Azeez is seeking to quash the IRB’s decision to unilaterally cancel the agreement dated February 9, 2022, and the subsequent notice of composite assessment dated March 22, 2022, involving the assessment years 2011 to 2020.
Among others, Abdul Azeez is contending that the agreement and subsequent composite assessment notice is final and conclusive per the law and is also asking for a court order compelling IRB to abide by said agreement.
Abdul Azeez claimed that the IRB had conducted a tax investigation against him in late 2021 or early 2022, which resulted in the agreement dated February 9, 2022.
He said under the agreement, both parties had agreed on the settlement of RM4.8 million in taxes and penalties for assessment years 2011 to 2020, adding that he had settled the amount through instalments as agreed.
Meanwhile, Nicholas submitted that the agreement was a written statutory agreement made pursuant to the power under Section 96A of the Income Tax Act 1967 and subsequently given effect through a formal composite assessment.
“Our position is that under Section 96A(6) of the Income Tax Act, once a composite assessment is made, it is final, conclusive and cannot simply be cancelled.
“This was not some letter written by a junior officer. It was a written statutory agreement, pursuant to power under the Act, which was then given effect by a formal assessment. It was signed by the respondent himself, the Director General of IRB at that time,” he said.
Justice Indra fixed November 11 to deliver her decision on the leave application. — Bernama

Title: Witness tells court he handed RM350,000 in cash to Hamzah Zainudin’s former aide over PDRM tender
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A witness told the Sessions Court here today that he met Sayed Amir Muzzakkir Al Sayed Mohamad, who is the former political secretary to former Home Minister Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin, to hand over RM350,000 in cash at the Yayasan Tanah Aku office in Publika in 2020.
Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, said he handed over RM100,000 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir at about 4pm on December 4, 2020, and RM250,000 at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020.
The 17th prosecution witness said this when re-examined by Deputy Public Prosecutor Hazel Tan Jia Qi at the trial of Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, who is facing three corruption charges involving RM350,000 in connection with a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender.
“I handed over RM100,000 in a paper bag to Sayed... and RM250,000, also in a paper bag, was handed over on December 16, 2020. During those handovers, it was just the two of us,” he said.
Wan Azhar also confirmed that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir had asked him, “Can you pay 350k? I need the money, in cash”.
He said the RM350,000 was part of a five per cent commission for assistance rendered to Nexuscorpgroup Sdn Bhd (NSB) in securing a PDRM project tender worth RM381.11 million.
Wan Azhar also said he referred to the five per cent as a commission rather than an “advisory fee”, based on a conversation between him and Al Khairi Group Bhd managing director Datuk Seri Mohd Khairi Mat Jahya before the “Project Advisory Agreement” between MKM Solutions Sdn Bhd and NSB was executed.
In his earlier witness statement, Wan Azhar confirmed that the agreement was drawn up to formalise a five per cent commission arrangement based on the project value, as requested by Sayed Amir Muzzakkir and Mohd Khairi.
On Sept 29, Wan Azhar denied a defence lawyer’s allegation that he had changed the term “advisory fee” in the “Project Advisory Agreement” to “commission” in his witness statement to link the case involving Sayed Amir Muzzakkir to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
On May 23, 2024, Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, 44, was charged on two counts of receiving RM350,000 in gratification from Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof as inducement for assisting NSB secure the tender for PDRM valued at RM381,112,042.44.
The offences were allegedly committed at the office of Yayasan Tanah Aku, Solaris Dutamas, here, at 4pm on December 4, 2020 and at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020, respectively.
Sayed Amir Muzzakkir was also charged with soliciting RM350,000 in gratification from the same individual, for a similar purpose, at the Shah Alam office of NSB in early December 2020.
The charges were framed under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment and a fine of not less than five times the value of the gratification or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The trial before Judge Rosli Ahmad resumes on November 11. — Bernama

Title: Jelutong MP urges govt to provide financial assistance to families of Malaysians missing in Nepal floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government has been urged to consider providing financial assistance to all Malaysian families whose relatives are still missing due to the floods and landslide disaster in Nepal last August.
The matter was proposed by Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer, who also urged the relevant departments or ministries to consider a moratorium on housing loans, personal bank loans, and vehicle purchases for all victims involved.
“I wish to appeal to the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), who will table the 2027 Budget tomorrow, to consider financial assistance for families of all affected victims,” he said at a press conference at the Parliament Building today.
Rayer also requested the National Registration Department (JPN) to facilitate the processing and issuance of documents such as death certificates to the affected families following the announcement that the Nepalese authorities will end search and rescue operations and declare the unrecovered victims as deceased.
Meanwhile, Rayer, who is also the Chairman of the Penang Hindu Endowment Board (PHEB), stated that the board has decided to provide a compassionate contribution of RM5,000 to each Hindu family of the tragedy victims who originate from Penang.
PHEB Deputy Chairman Senator Dr. R.A. Lingeshwaran said eligible families can apply for the assistance via a QR code displayed on PHEB’s official Facebook account and website.
A total of 54 Malaysians remain missing following the devastating floods and landslides that struck the Nepal-Tibet border region on August 26. — Bernama

Title: Why Malaysian professionals look to Singapore? Because many can earn more than double, says HR minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysian professionals could earn significantly higher working in neighbouring Singapore compared to just a median income of around RM6,000 here, according to a study, highlighting a stark wage disparity that Putrajaya is seeking to address through targeted tax incentives and wage growth initiatives.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan said in a written parliamentary reply that data from the Statistics Department’s 2025 wage survey placed the median monthly wage for professionals in Malaysia at RM6,124 ($1,430).
By contrast, a study by government agency TalentCorp showed that a majority of Malaysian professionals employed in Singapore earn between SG$4,001 (RM12,773) and SG$7,000 (RM22,348) per month.
“A 2024 study conducted by Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp) titled
Push and Pull Factors Influencing Malaysians to Work in Singapore and Proposes Relevant Policy Recommendations
found that 94.5 per cent of respondents cited higher salaries and better earning potential as the primary factor attracting them to work in Singapore,” the minister said.
The earnings gap is most pronounced in high-tech sectors, he added, with TalentCorp finding that skilled Malaysian professionals in Singapore can command monthly salaries exceeding SG$10,000 (RM31,926), particularly in information technology.
The Anwar government has deployed a progressive wage policy model designed to uplift workers earning below RM5,000 a month to curb talent outflow and boost local compensation.
Malaysia is also rolling out tax relief mechanisms under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), introducing a flat 15 per cent personal income tax rate for eligible knowledge workers employed by companies in the zone.
The tax incentive is aimed at inducing Singapore-based firms to relocate operations across the border to Johor, allowing businesses to optimise operational costs while offering higher salaries to local workers.
Malaysian professionals earning the national median wage of RM6,124 per month are typically subject to a standard personal income tax rate of 19 per cent.
Ramanan said Putrajaya is also utilising TalentCorp’s Returning Experts Programme which also features a flat 15 per cent tax rate as part of a broader strategy to incentivise Malaysian talent abroad to return home.

Title: E-hailing driver claims trial to driving under influence of drugs, causing Maldivian student’s death on LDP
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — An e-hailing driver today claimed trial in the Magistrate’s Court here to three charges, including causing the death of a Maldivian student in an accident on Sunday.
Muhamad Syafiq Ibrahim, 37, pleaded not guilty to the charges read out to him before Magistrate Muhammad Syafiq Sulaiman.
According to the charges, the father of two was alleged to have driven a Perodua Ativa under the influence of methamphetamine, resulting in the death of his passenger, Aamina Imeely Nazim, 22.
He was also charged with driving the same vehicle under the influence of the same drug, resulting in injuries to another Maldivian passenger, Aishath Sara Nizam, 22.
He was further charged with driving the vehicle without due care and attention, causing an accident involving another vehicle and injuring Aishath Sara.
All three offences were allegedly committed on the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP), near the PJS Toll Plaza, at about 8.40pm on Sunday.
The first charge was framed under Section 44(1)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum prison term of 15 years and a fine of between RM50,000 and RM100,000 upon conviction.
The second charge was framed under Section 44(1A)(a) of the same act, which carries a maximum prison term of 10 years and a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.
The third charge, under Section 43(1) of the act, carries a maximum prison term of 12 months and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000 upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan proposed bail of RM10,000 in one surety for each charge, but lawyer Rohan Singh appealed for the amount to be reduced, saying his client earned only about RM2,000 a month as an e-hailing driver and that his wife was a homemaker.
The court allowed bail of RM9,000 in one surety, suspended his driving licence until the case is concluded and fixed December 4 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia needs highly skilled talent to support shift to high-value economy, says Zambry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Malaysia needs skilled talent to support its transition to a high-value economy, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said.
He said the country has several policies and plans to develop highly skilled talent, including the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint 2026-2035, the 13th Malaysia Plan and the National Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Policy 2030.
“We want industries to move further up the value chain. We want high-growth sectors to expand. We want quality investments to bring in technology and better jobs.
“However, there can be no economic transformation without talent transformation. We can bring in the best technology and develop the most advanced infrastructure, but ultimately, everything depends on people with the knowledge, skills and values to drive it,” he said.
He said this in a speech delivered by Higher Education Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Aminuddin Hassim at the Industry Nexus (INDEX) 2026: TVET Collaboration Hub programme here today.
Zambry said INDEX is more than a platform that brings institutions and industry together; it connects industry needs with the strengths of higher education.
“We want this relationship to move beyond mere engagement towards creating things together. Industry should not simply be at the end of the chain as a recipient of graduates, but work with institutions to identify needs, develop competencies, bring in technology and provide opportunities for real-world experience.
“In other words, we need to move from relationships to collaboration, and from collaboration to value creation,” he said.
Meanwhile, Zambry said polytechnics and community colleges (POLYCC) must keep strengthening high-impact programmes with clear links to growth sectors and industry needs.
“The principle is simple. Do not develop programmes first and then ask industry whether it needs graduates. Identify industry needs first, then develop the programmes and talent together.
“This approach is important in addressing the skills mismatch. We cannot be satisfied when graduates secure jobs,” he said. — Bernama

Title: National Climate Change Bill to institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting, says Arthur Kurup
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The proposed National Climate Change Bill will institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting and clear governance to give businesses the legal certainty needed to decarbonise.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the legislation, alongside the National Climate Change Policy 2.0, would align Malaysia’s environmental agenda with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030).
He said the measure would also strengthen investor confidence and encourage domestic and international investment in clean technologies.
“With our upcoming National Climate Change Bill, we will institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting and clear governance to give businesses the legal certainty they need to decarbonise,” he said in his opening remarks at the 17th International Greentech and Eco Products Exhibition and Conference Malaysia (IGEM) 2026, held alongside the Kuala Lumpur Sustainability Summit (KLSS) 2026 at Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre, today.
The event was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who is also Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation.
Arthur said the National Carbon Market Policy, launched in April, established a transparent and high-integrity regulatory framework for voluntary and compliance markets, with clear Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) standards aligned with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.
He said the policy would provide domestic developers and global investors with the regulatory certainty needed to trade carbon credits, particularly in driving decarbonisation across hard-to-abate sectors.
“Through the Green Technology Financing Scheme 5.0, we support the industry by providing government guarantees that help reduce financing risks and ease access to financing for green projects,” he said.
He noted that the scheme, together with the Green Investment Tax Allowance, would improve the viability of green investments and give project developers greater confidence to turn green ambitions into bankable projects.
He said the Malaysian Green Technology and Climate Change Corporation (MGTC) was also expanding practical tools such as the MyHIJAU Mark to verify green products and services, while enabling Malaysian businesses to access government green procurement and high-value green supply chains across Asean.
At the sub-national level, Arthur said the ministry was working with state governments and local authorities to accelerate green technology adoption, including through the Low Carbon Cities Framework, which enables local councils to measure, manage and reduce urban emissions.
He said IGEM and KLSS complemented each other by connecting green technologies with industry and local leaders, while bringing regulators, financiers and thought leaders together on governance, taxonomy and transition finance needed to scale green technologies.
The minister said IGEM had generated more than RM86 billion in business leads and attracted over 700,000 global participants since its inception, while IGEM 2025, held alongside the inaugural KLSS, generated RM7.3 billion in potential green investments through structured business-matching sessions.
The 17th edition of IGEM, themed “Race Towards Net Zero: Action Beyond Boundaries”, is being held from October 7 to 9.  It is organised by the NRES and its agency, MGTC. — Bernama

Title: Anwar personally contacts Indonesian President Prabowo over haze crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today he has personally contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto regarding the “alarming” level of transboundary haze affecting Malaysia and the region.
Speaking to reporters at an impromptu press conference outside the Finance Ministry today, he said the relevant ministries are also in contact with their regional counterparts to address the problem.
“The matter of the haze is at an alarming level and I’ve personally contacted President Prabowo, and he has agreed to take the necessary steps,” Anwar said.
He said the government is concerned about the impact on the health of Malaysians and has therefore stepped up the frequency of cloud seeding in an effort to mitigate the situation, notwithstanding unsatisfactory recent results.
His remarks come as the Department of Environment (DOE) reported that 38 areas in Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index readings at 3pm today.
The DOE, citing the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre, said 94 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan and 210 in Sumatra on Oct 7, with moderate to dense transboundary haze observed over southern and central Sumatra, Singapore and the southern Peninsula.
Earlier today, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, urged authorities to close schools in areas with elevated API readings of over 150.

Title: Selangor govt, state Education Dept to discuss measures to address haze and Super El Nino, says MB
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari will meet the State Education Department (JPNS) tomorrow to discuss follow-up measures regarding the haze situation currently affecting the state.
He said the meeting would look into the necessary measures, including those involving school operations, based on developments in air quality and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and Department of Environment (DOE).
“I am waiting for the final meteorological report to see how much longer this situation is expected to last. We have plans to provide assistance, for example, to special education schools. We will see how the situation develops over the next day or two, as the school session will end around November, before the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examinations.
“I will meet JPNS tomorrow to look at what immediate follow-up measures we can take. However, we have a standard, meaning that if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading reaches 200, we will close schools,” he said.
He said this after presenting aid to 500 recipients under the Jelajah Sejahtera Madani — Skim Insurans Kesejahteraan Rakyat (SIKR) 3.0 programme at the Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC), here today.
He said follow-up measures would be coordinated with JPNS in accordance with the prescribed standard operating procedures (SOPs) should air quality deteriorate further, while the state administration would also continue to strengthen coordination with relevant technical agencies to ensure public safety and health on an ongoing basis.
“In fact, what is more concerning is the period from around February to April next year, as the Super El Nino phenomenon is forecast to persist until April. This is the beginning of the hot season, and we may face hot weather and a lack of rainfall.
“Close monitoring is crucial to ensure that any preventive measures can be implemented without affecting the academic schedule or the safety of students,” he said.
In another development, Amirudin said the raw water supply in Selangor remained stable and sufficient to meet domestic needs ahead of the monsoon transition phase.
He said based on cumulative data to date, the state’s water supply could last for a minimum of three months to a maximum of nine months, depending on weather conditions and rainfall.
Earlier, Amirudin launched the Jelajah Sejahtera Madani — SIKR 3.0 programme, a strategic collaboration between the Implementation Coordination Unit, Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM), and Prudential BSN Takaful Berhad (PruBSN).
A total of RM20 million has been allocated to provide 12 months of insurance coverage to 250,000 heads of households (KIR) from poor and hardcore poor families registered in the eKasih system, against mishaps such as death, accidents and permanent disability.
The initiative also includes free health screenings for 500 households through PruBSN Prihatin.
The comprehensive initiative aims to strengthen the social safety net, help families facing hardships, and support the Madani Government’s aspiration towards social stability and the sustained well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Hazy math: DoE explains why your AQI says 250 when the official API is 175
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has clarified that higher air quality figures displayed on independent mobile applications and third-party websites do not reflect data suppression or inaccuracies in official records
Just as 38 areas in Malaysia logged unhealthy air quality today, the department explained that Malaysia’s Air Pollutant Index (API) and commercial Air Quality Index (AQI) platforms frequently show divergent numbers because they rely on different index scales, mathematical models, concentration thresholds, averaging durations, update intervals, and sensory inputs.
Many international applications employ the US AQI standard or rely on low-cost uncalibrated sensors, predictive computational models, or satellite imagery.
Satellite monitoring, the DOE pointed out, evaluates total aerosol column density across the upper atmosphere rather than air quality at ground level where human respiration occurs. Importantly, satellite sensors can misidentify atmospheric cloud cover or water vapour as particulate haze.
The department stressed that valid comparisons between platforms cannot be drawn from single headline figures alone, but must match identical geographic coordinates and time stamps, direct pollutant concentrations, and specific indexing methodologies.
The DOE advised the public to rely on verified data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) web portal or the MyJAS EQMS mobile application.
These platforms update hourly and serve as the government’s official benchmark for health advisories and disaster response protocols.
Malaysia’s national API is calculated using continuous measurements of six core criteria pollutants, with fine particulate matter (PM2.5) acting as the dominant driver during haze events.
The system draws data from 68 continuous monitoring stations nationwide that comply with strict ISO standards and US Environmental Protection Agency guidelines.
Unhealthy air quality blankets 38 areas
As of 3pm today, no monitoring stations in the country recorded good air quality, with 30 stations registering moderate levels and 38 falling into the unhealthy category (API 101 to 200).
Southern and central states recorded the most severe pollution levels, led by Segamat at 190, Seremban at 186, Nilai at 185, and Kluang at 181. Rompin in Pahang and peat fire hotspot Johan Setia in Selangor each logged 178, while the administrative centre of Putrajaya recorded 175.
Across the Greater Klang Valley, elevated readings were recorded in Cheras (174), Shah Alam (171), and Petaling Jaya (165). Unhealthy air quality was also recorded across monitoring stations in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Melaka, and Terengganu, where Paka registered the lowest reading in the unhealthy bracket at 126.
The DOE attributed the deteriorating air quality to prolonged dry spells across the southern Asean region.
Citing data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC), the department noted that 210 fire hotspots were detected in Sumatra and 94 in Kalimantan on Oct 7, compared to just one localized hotspot in Pahang, Malaysia.
The ASMC observed moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes drifting across central and southern Sumatra, Singapore, and southern Peninsular Malaysia.
Under the National Haze Action Plan, all outdoor school activities must be suspended immediately when local API readings surpass 100. Should readings exceed the 200 threshold, schools, kindergartens, and daycare centres are ordered to close.
If API levels remain consistently above 150 for more than 24 hours, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) convenes its disaster coordination committee to assess cloud seeding operations, subject to suitable atmospheric moisture and cloud conditions.

Title: King calls for schools to close if API stays above 150-180 for prolonged period
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim has called for schools in haze-hit areas to close if Air Pollutant Index (API) readings go above a range of 150 to 180 for a prolonged period.
The King expressed concern over the health and safety of schoolchildren and students amid the haze affecting the country, urging the Education Ministry to give serious attention to the situation.
“Appropriate measures must be taken by the relevant ministries and agencies to protect schoolchildren and students, including senior citizens and patients with respiratory illnesses.
“Always take precautions to safeguard your health, including wearing face masks and reducing outdoor activities due to the haze,” His Majesty said.
Sultan Ibrahim stressed that the health and safety of schoolchildren and students must be given priority amid the deteriorating air quality.
Yesterday, Johor announced the closure of schools for two days on the decree of Tunku Mahkota Ismail, Regent of Johor, following worsening haze and air quality across the state.

Title: Dapat Vista responds to PAC findings, backs urgent completion of formal eJamin agreement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Dapat Vista (M) Sdn Bhd, the operator of the eJamin court bail payment system, has acknowledged the findings and recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee and supports the urgent completion of a formal agreement with the government.
The company, a subsidiary of Pertama Digital Berhad, said the agreement would strengthen accountability and enhance safeguards for bail funds while maintaining continuity of service for the courts and the public.
Dapat Vista and Pertama Digital Berhad made the remarks in a joint statement issued today.
“Public confidence matters to us, and we continue to take our responsibility to bailors seriously,” the companies said.
“eJamin continues to operate, with refunds and forfeitures processed in accordance with applicable court orders.”
The companies said they remain committed to working closely with the relevant authorities to complete the formal agreement, which will set out clear responsibilities and safeguards for bail funds.
They added that they have cooperated throughout engagements with authorities and will continue to provide records, information and clarification required to address matters raised by the PAC.
The eJamin service was launched in January 2020 by the then Chief Justice to simplify court bail payments.
It enables bailors to make payments online, reducing the need to travel between courts and banks.
Engagements on eJamin began in 2019 and continued through 2024 and 2025, with an interim special exemption granted in November 2024 and extended in May 2025.
Dapat Vista said the formal agreement is at the final government approval stage, with the current Ministry of Finance special exemption extending until December 31, 2026, or until the agreement is concluded and executed, whichever is earlier.
The company said eJamin operates as a public-private partnership model without development, operating or maintenance fees paid by the government or the public.
Under the existing funding model, bail funds not required for daily refunds are placed in current account deposit and investment arrangements through approved financial institutions, including Islamic instruments.
Only the interest income generated from these investments is made available to Dapat Vista to fund the operation of the eJamin system, with the current operating cost averaging RM450,000 per month.
Dapat Vista said the RM557,258 difference noted by the PAC relates to the reconciliation of balances as at December 31, 2024, and arose from funds in transit — transactions recorded in the eJamin system that had not yet cleared or appeared in the corresponding bank statements at the cut-off date.
The company said it has documented and reported its explanation to the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court, the Prime Minister’s Department and the Accountant General’s Department, and has provided the supporting records required to complete and verify the reconciliation.

Title: Zambry: MOHE targets 30,000 AI graduates by 2030 to meet future workforce needs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE) aims to produce 30,000 graduates skilled in artificial intelligence (AI) between 2025 and 2030 to address the challenges of automation and meet future workforce needs.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir said the target would be achieved through 30 specialised programmes at bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral (PhD) levels currently offered at 11 public universities.
He said to ensure that academic programmes remained relevant to technological advancements, 455 programmes across various levels had undergone a review as of Sept 30.
“For specialised AI programmes, development and accreditation have also been strengthened through the Programme Standards: Artificial Intelligence (PS:AI) developed by the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA), to ensure that they are developed systematically and meet the stipulated quality standards,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said this in reply to a question from Datuk Seri Dr Shahidan Kassim (PN-Arau) on measures taken by MOHE to ensure graduates possess AI skills to cope with changes in the job market, following expectations that many jobs could be at risk of being replaced by automation.
Elaborating, Zambry said the talent development ecosystem was also being strengthened through the establishment of the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM), the Faculty of Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM), and the Faculty of Intelligent Computing at Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP).
To ensure that graduates remained competitive and their employability was maintained, he said MOHE planned to integrate AI elements into 80 per cent of bachelor’s degree courses at public universities.
“We are also implementing upskilling programmes, work-based learning and stackable programmes to ensure that AI skills can be developed at every level of study, enabling our graduates to remain employable when they graduate from university,” he said.
Responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Shahelmey Yahya (BN-Putatan) on students’ critical thinking skills, which he said were increasingly being eroded by the ‘ask ChatGPT’ mentality, Zambry said the biggest challenge facing universities today was to strike a balance in using AI as a learning aid rather than as an agent that completely takes over human thinking.
“Agentic AI is the latest development in our world. It has become humanoid (human-like), meaning it can think for us, solve problems for us, and can even understand feelings.
“This is very dangerous. That is why the measures being taken are aimed at striking a balance so that our higher education system can produce well-rounded, comprehensive, and holistic individuals,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia strengthens space disaster SOPs, prepares for risk of falling space objects, says Chang Lih Kang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia is strengthening the country’s preparedness to deal with potential incidents involving falling space objects, including satellite or rocket debris, through simulation exercises and improvements to disaster operating procedures.
Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said the effort included the implementation of the Space Accident Simulation Exercise (ExLAKA), which serves as a platform to test and assess the country’s response capabilities in the event of a space object falling incident.
“The ministry conducted ExLAKA Phase 1 on November 26 and 27 last year, while Phase 2, involving a more complex scenario, was conducted on October 1.
“The full-scale exercise is expected to be held in early 2027,” he said in reply to a supplementary question from Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng) on the country’s preparedness for space accident incidents during the oral question-and-answer session in Parliament today.
He said the assessment results and findings from the overall exercises would be used to improve the Space Disaster Standard Operating Procedures (PTO) 4.0.
Chang stressed that the measure was important to ensure that all relevant agencies had clearer and better-coordinated procedures in the event of an accident involving a space object.
Meanwhile, he said Investigation Document Version 3.0, which details the investigation process for the discovery of objects suspected to be space objects, had also been updated based on the actual experience of the Space Authority Division (BPAngkasa) in the field.
Chang said coordination had also been strengthened when a meeting on January 28 this year officially included space accident incidents under the National Disaster Management Agency’s (Nadma) Directive No. 1.
“With this, affected victims are eligible to receive Nadma social financial assistance, while operational costs are borne by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti) under BPAngkasa,” he said.
He said Mosti also planned to establish a National Trust Account for environmental restoration purposes in the event of an incident requiring remedial action.
He said that apart from disaster response, coordination of airspace management was also being given attention, with BPAngkasa participating in the Joint Airspace Industry Committee (JIB RUA) and Technical Airspace Committee (JT RUA) led by the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) and Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
“This is to manage traffic in the airspace-space segment and launch clearances, while (BPAngkasa) is being considered for permanent membership,” he said. — Bernama

Title: King grants audience to IPCC chairman at Istana Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today granted an audience to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) chairman Datuk Zolkopli Dahalan and deputy chairman Martina@Kartina Zamhari at Istana Negara here.
During the nearly hour-long audience, His Majesty was briefed on the commission’s role, functions and powers.
“His Majesty also received a briefing on the statistics of complaints that the IPCC received, as well as the status and outcomes of cases that have been resolved,” according to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page today.
According to the post, the IPCC, which began operating on Nov 1, 2023, is responsible for independently, transparently and with integrity monitoring, investigating and handling complaints of misconduct and breaches of conduct involving Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel.
The commission also makes recommendations to improve the welfare and wellbeing of police personnel. — Bernama

Title: Myanmar president departs Malaysia after two-day visit focused on repatriation, bilateral ties
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 8 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing departed for home this afternoon after concluding a two-day official visit to Malaysia.
Min Aung Hlaing was given a red-carpet ceremonial send-off and a guard-of-honour by the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment, led by Capt Wan Muhammad Amirul Syafiq Wan Zamri at Bunga Raya Complex (BRC) of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) here.
His delegation boarded a special flight at 2.10pm. They were sent off by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, who was the minister in attendance for the visit.
Min Aung Hlaing, who arrived yesterday, was accorded an official welcome at the Perdana Putra Complex in Putrajaya this morning.
After the ceremony, he proceeded to have a four-eyed meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, followed by a delegation meeting before attending a luncheon hosted by Anwar.
During the meetings, Malaysia and Myanmar agreed to strengthen bilateral ties, prioritise people-centric cooperation, and support Myanmar’s efforts to pursue reforms and policy adjustments aimed at addressing the country’s complex challenges.
The visit also resulted in Myanmar agreeing to accept the large-scale repatriation of its nationals at its own expense.
Speaking at a joint press conference, Anwar said more than 10,493 Myanmar citizens and personnel had so far been repatriated to Myanmar through flights and naval ships, with further repatriation to be negotiated between Malaysia’s Ministry of Home Affairs and its Myanmar counterpart.
He said the remaining Myanmar nationals would be repatriated according to the stipulated rules and procedures, subject to verification of their records.
Economic ties between Malaysia and Myanmar also showed significant potential, with bilateral economic activities increasing by more than 140 per cent year-on-year. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng urges Anwar to deliver tangible economic relief, raise tax threshold to RM12,000 in likely ‘final’ pre-election Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to use Budget 2027 to deliver tangible economic relief, calling it the administration’s final realistic opportunity to win over voters before the next general election.
Lim proposed raising the personal income tax relief threshold to RM12,000 from the current RM9,000 to offset cumulative inflation, noting that the relief limit has remained unchanged for 17 years.
Speaking to media in Parliament ahead of the official Budget 2027 presentation, the former finance minister stressed that while a national Budget will be tabled in late 2027, its measures will not take effect quickly enough to influence the electorate before the government’s term expires.
Lim said that while he believed Anwar could still table the Budget before Parliament is dissolved, any attempt to win over voters would not be as effective as “it would be too late”.
“All our proposals are necessary. If not, I am worried this would be the last chance for the Madani government to make the Budget’s benefit tangible to the people,” he said.
“Yes, I believe he could still table another Budget, but I feel the impact will not be the same since it would be too late.”
Anwar acknowledged the economic strain on households in a social media post recently, stating that macroeconomic growth alone is insufficient and pledging that the upcoming fiscal plan will directly address cost-of-living pressures and distribute economic gains more equitably.
Malaysia’s current Parliament first convened on December 19, 2022, and its five-year term automatically expires in December 2027, requiring a general election to be held within 60 days unless Parliament is dissolved earlier.
Lim said there is typically a Cabinet meeting held before the tabling of the Budget, noting that in the past, last-minute additions have been made at such meetings.
“We suggest raising the personal tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000. The threshold for this relief has not changed for 17 years and if we account for inflation, RM9,000 in 2010 is now RM12,000.
In addition to personal income tax adjustments, Lim called for a RM1,000 increase in tax relief allocations for both education and healthcare expenses to assist middle-class families.
The DAP leader also advocated for targeted support for eldercare, appealing to the government to abolish the 8 per cent service tax recently imposed on private old-age homes to reduce the financial burden on caregivers.

Title: Anwar-Min Aung Hlaing talks focus on refugees, not recognition of Myanmar govt, says Fahmi
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s meeting with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today does not constitute recognition of the country’s government but is aimed at resolving the longstanding issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the meeting reflected the government’s use of diplomatic channels to address domestic concerns, particularly those involving Myanmar refugees.
“This meeting does not mean we recognise the Myanmar government. It is intended to find a solution to the longstanding issue of Myanmar refugees in our country,” he said at the opening of the Inanam Sentral National Information Dissemination Centre (NADI) here today.
Fahmi also expressed hope that the meeting would yield positive results, including facilitating the return of Myanmar refugees through proper channels.
“We hope the Prime Minister’s meeting with the Myanmar President today will produce positive outcomes, allowing refugees from Myanmar’s 19 ethnic groups in Malaysia to return to their country through proper channels and helping us address the issues we face domestically,” he said.
Fahmi, who is also Madani Government spokesperson, also highlighted another important meeting scheduled for tomorrow after the tabling of Budget 2027, with discussions expected to cover efforts to strengthen bilateral ties and issues concerning Palestine.
“Let us await the outcomes of these two important meetings taking place today and tomorrow,” he said.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi is scheduled to make a state visit to Malaysia from October 9 to 10. — Bernama

Title: Loke urges Malaysian ports to speed up green transition with electric terminal trucks
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 8 — Domestic port operators have been urged to accelerate their decarbonisation initiatives, including the adoption of electric terminal trucks (e-prime movers) for port operations, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
He said the shift towards greener practices aligns with Malaysia’s commitment under the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.
“Carbon reduction efforts at the port’s operational level must keep pace with the global shipping industry's transition, which is currently exploring the use of alternative fuels such as methanol, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and ammonia
“The use of electric-powered machinery, such as the e-prime movers implemented by the Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), aligns with that objective.
“With that, I am confident that other port operators will follow suit. However, it still remains at the discretion of the port operators, as it involves investment and new assets on their part,” he told reporters after launching an electric terminal truck fleet at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas here today.
Also present were Johor Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh and PTP chief executive officer Mark Hardiman.
Loke said greater compliance with environmental, social and governance (ESG) standards would enable local ports to operate more responsibly while maintaining their competitiveness and strengthening their position in the global shipping industry.
“The Transport Ministry is committed to establishing policies and regulatory framework to support this green initiatives.
“We are also collaborating with the Australian government to formulate regulations regarding the supply of green fuel and to fine-tune standard operating procedures (SOPs) at ports,” he said.
He added that the transition to electric-powered machinery would also require supporting infrastructure, including charging stations and new safety protocols, to ensure smooth terminal operations.
Meanwhile, Loke commended the consolidation of PTP and Pasir Gudang Port under the ‘Johor Port’ brand, which he said had helped the combined port operations achieve a ranking of 11th among the world’s busiest ports.
He said Johor’s port facilities, comprising PTP and Pasir Gudang Port, handled more than 14 million containers annually.
“This achievement propelled its ranking to 11th place among the world’s busiest ports, placing it just behind Port Klang, which currently holds the 10th spot.
“PTP possesses immense potential to be developed into the nation’s largest green bunkering and transhipment hub.
“We hope this initiative will attract further investment and stimulate economic activity in the areas surrounding Tanjung Pelepas,” he said. — Bernama pic

Title: Malaysia to strengthen AI training modules as deepfake, scam risks grow, says Gobind
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Digital Ministry will continue to strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) training modules based on newly identified risks, including deepfake threats and the misuse of the technology.
Its Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the effort was being carried out through AI Malaysia Bhd, which also has an AI Safe initiative involving experts to examine security aspects and identify preventive measures against emerging technology threats.
“This is indeed something being monitored by AI Malaysia Bhd and it is a work in progress. We will ensure that each module is further strengthened whenever we identify new risks and the measures that can be taken to prevent people from falling victim to such risks,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said this in reply to a supplementary question from Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) on measures taken by the government to address the risks of AI use among civil servants, as well as the misuse of the technology, including deepfakes, voice cloning, fake videos and AI-based scams.
He added that the training modules offered to various segments of society also included explanations of the risks associated with using new technologies, as well as ways to prevent users from falling victim to their misuse.
He said the aspect was also incorporated into the Executive Digital Leadership Programme (EDLP) and the use of Gemini Workspace in the public sector to ensure that civil servants understood the risks arising from the development of AI.
Responding to a supplementary question from Tan Hong Pin (PH-Bakri) on the role of AI Malaysia Bhd in expanding AI talent and skills development, particularly among youths, Gobind said the effort required collaboration among various parties, including the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education, industry and academic institutions.
He said AI Malaysia Bhd was responsible for identifying the country’s talent needs, compiling information on existing training modules and assessing their suitability to industry requirements and target groups.
The effort was also aimed at identifying existing training gaps so that new modules could be developed to meet the needs of people across various segments of society.
Gobind said the ministry was currently in the process of establishing a structure that would enable AI Malaysia Bhd to carry out the role comprehensively, while ensuring that AI talent development initiatives reached people who needed new skills. — Bernama
